literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: RSV 季节于 2022 年 2 月中旬开始。RT-PCR 确诊的病例中有 54% (25/46) 报告有一种或多种症状,其中 26% (12/46) 报告发烧,37% (17/46) 报告咳嗽。中位 RNA 脱落持续时间为 7 天(IQR = 4-11 天)。 [10.1111/irv.70308]
2018 年至 2023 年期间,在 60 岁以上的成年人中发现了 42 例 RSV 编码住院病例。年年龄和性别标准化 RSV 编码住院率显示出显着的逐年变化。在RSV编码入院的患者中,中位住院时间为11天(IQR 6-18),四名患者(9.52%)在住院期间死亡。 [10.1111/irv.70315]
结果表明,参与者能够描述 RSV 感染的 流行病学,讨论 65 岁及以上成年人和患有高危疾病的年轻人的临床表现和结果,并解决诊断挑战和当前的 治疗 选择。 [10.1016/j.jen.2026.03.008]

在出生后的前五周,与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,宽限期内使用 mAb 策略使 RSV 住院风险加倍(aHR:2.0 [95% CI:1.0-4.9]),并增加就医 RSV 风险(aHR:1.6 [95% CI:1.0-2.7])。与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,mAb 预期策略的 RSV 住院风险相似 (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9])。 [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361361]
体内研究表明,槐花生物碱通过气管内给药可显着降低 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率。在小鼠模型中,负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。 [10.1016/j.colsurfb.2026.115697]

During 2018–2023, 42 RSV‐coded hospitalizations were identified among adults aged ≥ 60 years. Annual age‐ and sex‐standardized RSV‐coded hospitalization rates showed substantial year‐to‐year variability. [10.1111/irv.70315]

The results indicated that participants were able to describe the epidemiology of RSV infection, discuss its clinical presentation and outcomes in adults aged 65 years and older and younger adults with high-risk conditions, and address diagnostic challenges and current treatment options. [10.1016/j.jen.2026.03.008]
Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). [10.1001/jamainternmed.2026.3841]

In the first five weeks of life, the mAb within grace period strategy doubled the hazard of RSV hospitalization (aHR: 2.0 [95% CI: 1.0-4.9]) and increased the hazard of medically-attended RSV (aHR: 1.6 [95% CI: 1.0-2.7]) compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy. [10.64898/2026.08.25.26361361]

key_findings_en: The UK's NHS Wales extended the RSV vaccine offer to higher-risk adults aged 65–74 as part of a time-limited programme. This decision was based on evidence showing similar hospitalisation risks for this age group compared to those aged over 75. [news-dfb7c52d71217945]
The CDC published a report on respiratory virus activity levels, including Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). [news-31e57dad649983cf]

Real-world data showed that mRNA-1345 RSV vaccination is associated with a reduced risk for RSV-confirmed acute respiratory illness hospitalization in US veterans, as reported in a study published in Vaccine. [news-fddb3958281f89e7]

papers.title: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination for infant protection: updated systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy, effectiveness, and safety
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe illness in infants and young children. Methods We updated this systematic review to explore the efficacy, effectiveness and safety of authorised maternal RSV prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccine for infant protection. We searched MEDLINE, Cochrane Library/Central, Embase and grey literature from 2000 to June 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs). Results Meta-analyses of RCTs showed high certainty of evidence that maternal RSVpreF vaccine lowered medically attended RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections (RSV-LRTI) with vaccine efficacy of 68% (relative risk (RR) 0.32; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.13 to 0.77, 2 trials; 7656 participants), severe RSV-LRTI with a vaccine efficacy of 84% (RR 0.16; 95% CI 0.07 to 0.36, 2 trials; 7656 participants) and RSV-related hospitalisations with a vaccine efficacy of 70% (RR 0.30; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.61, 1 trial; 7148 participants) in infants. Within the limited evidence base available, there may be little to no difference in RSV-related mortality, all-cause mortality, vaccine-related serious adverse events, and intensive care admission. Requirements for invasive ventilation and duration of hospitalisation due to RSV disease were not reported by any trials. NRSIs suggested effectiveness of 72% (RR 0.28; 95% CI: 0.17 to 0.46, 3 NRSIs; 1229 participants) against hospitalisation, but certainty was very low. Interpretation Maternal RSVpreF vaccination reduced medically attended and severe RSV-LRTI and RSV-related hospitalisation in infants. No safety signals were identified. Further research is required to clarify the long-term effectiveness of the authorised vaccine.

papers.title_original: Maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination for infant protection: updated systematic review and meta-analysis of efficacy, effectiveness, and safety

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; Orthopneumovirus hominis, including RSV-A and RSV-B) as a cause of severe illness in infants and young children, focusing on maternal vaccination with the RSV prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccine to protect infants from RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections (RSV-LRTI), severe RSV-LRTI, and RSV-related hospitalizations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is an updated systematic review that searched MEDLINE, Cochrane Library/Central, Embase, and grey literature from 2000 to June 2025. It included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs) to assess efficacy, effectiveness, and safety of maternal RSVpreF vaccination for infant protection.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Meta-analyses of RCTs demonstrated high certainty that maternal RSVpreF vaccination significantly reduced medically attended RSV-LRTI (vaccine efficacy 68%, RR 0.32; 95% CI 0.13 to 0.77), severe RSV-LRTI (84%, RR 0.16; 95% CI 0.07 to 0.36), and RSV-related hospitalizations (70%, RR 0.30; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.61) in infants. Interpretation indicates maternal vaccination reduced these outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence gaps include the absence of reported data on requirements for invasive ventilation and duration of hospitalisation due to RSV disease in trials. NRSIs suggested effectiveness against hospitalisation (72%, RR 0.28; 95% CI 0.17 to 0.46) but with very low certainty. Long-term effectiveness of the authorised vaccine remains unclear.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priorities include clarifying long-term effectiveness of maternal RSVpreF vaccination and addressing evidence gaps such as invasive ventilation requirements and hospitalisation duration. Surveillance and monitoring for rare adverse events should continue to ensure safety.

analysis.summary_en: This updated systematic review evaluates maternal respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccination for protecting infants against RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections (RSV-LRTI), severe RSV-LRTI, and hospitalizations. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials show high-certainty evidence that maternal vaccination reduces medically attended RSV-LRTI by 68%, severe RSV-LRTI by 84%, and RSV-related hospitalizations by 70%. Non-randomised studies suggest effectiveness against hospitalisation at 72%, though with very low certainty. Key gaps include missing data on invasive ventilation needs and hospitalisation duration, and uncertainty about long-term vaccine effectiveness. The review concludes maternal RSVpreF vaccination is effective for infant protection and highlights the need for further research to address these gaps and ensure sustained protection.

papers.title_zh: 母体呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)预融合F(RSVpreF)疫苗对婴儿保护作用:更新的系统综述和荟萃分析评估其有效性、效果和安全性
papers.source_body_en: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe illness in infants and young children. Methods We updated this systematic review to explore the efficacy, effectiveness and safety of authorised maternal RSV prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccine for infant protection. We searched MEDLINE, Cochrane Library/Central, Embase and grey literature from 2000 to June 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and non-randomised studies of interventions (NRSIs). Results Meta-analyses of RCTs showed high certainty of evidence that maternal RSVpreF vaccine lowered medically attended RSV-related lower respiratory tract infections (RSV-LRTI) with vaccine efficacy of 68% (relative risk (RR) 0.32; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.13 to 0.77, 2 trials; 7656 participants), severe RSV-LRTI with a vaccine efficacy of 84% (RR 0.16; 95% CI 0.07 to 0.36, 2 trials; 7656 participants) and RSV-related hospitalisations with a vaccine efficacy of 70% (RR 0.30; 95% CI 0.15 to 0.61, 1 trial; 7148 participants) in infants. Within the limited evidence base available, there may be little to no difference in RSV-related mortality, all-cause mortality, vaccine-related serious adverse events, and intensive care admission. Requirements for invasive ventilation and duration of hospitalisation due to RSV disease were not reported by any trials. NRSIs suggested effectiveness of 72% (RR 0.28; 95% CI: 0.17 to 0.46, 3 NRSIs; 1229 participants) against hospitalisation, but certainty was very low. Interpretation Maternal RSVpreF vaccination reduced medically attended and severe RSV-LRTI and RSV-related hospitalisation in infants. No safety signals were identified. Further research is required to clarify the long-term effectiveness of the authorised vaccine.

papers.title: Seasonal dynamics and burden of respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and COVID-19 in Brazil: a national surveillance study (2019–2023)
papers.abstract: Background: The burden and seasonal patterns of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and COVID-19 remain poorly characterised in Brazil and other Latin American countries. Understanding their epidemiological patterns is essential to inform public health interventions and preventive strategies. We aimed to assess respiratory virus seasonality using national surveillance data to guide vaccination timing and strengthen preparedness strategies in Brazil. Methods: We conducted a retrospective, observational, descriptive population-based study using national surveillance data collected through the SIVEP system between 2019 and 2023. We analysed confirmed cases, hospitalisations, and deaths attributed to RSV, influenza, and COVID-19. We performed time-series decomposition and seasonal trend analysis using the multiple seasonal-trend decomposition via locally estimated scatterplot smoothing method. We calculated monthly mean values for each aetiology component to assess their seasonal burden. Results: There were 69,389 RSV, 45,881 influenza, and 2,299,712 COVID-19 cases among the laboratory-confirmed severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases reported in SIVEP. Each year, more than 90% of RSV diagnoses were reported in children aged 0-10 years, while influenza and COVID-19 were more common among older adults. The proportion of deaths in children related to RSV increased from 19.2% in 2020 to 62.0% in 2023. Seasonal peaks occurred from March to June for RSV, influenza cases peaked in January, while COVID-19 showed less consistent seasonality. Geographic variation was observed, with higher case concentrations in the Southeast and South regions of Brazil. Conclusions: The burden of respiratory viruses among SARI cases reported in the national surveillance system in Brazil differed by pathogen, age group, region, and season, and may be influenced by variations in testing strategies. Strengthening diagnostic capacity and surveillance is critical, particularly for adult RSV cases, which are likely underreported due to limited testing and reduced diagnostic sensitivity. Seasonal vaccination programmes, such as those for influenza, remain essential and may be further enhanced by integrating new preventive measures, such as RSV vaccination for older adults and maternal immunisation to protect infants.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在巴西和其他拉丁美洲国家,呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、流感和 COVID-19 的负担和季节性模式仍然不明确。了解其流行病学模式对于为公共卫生干预措施和预防策略提供信息至关重要。我们的目的是使用国家 监测 数据评估呼吸道病毒的季节性,以指导 疫苗接种 时间安排并加强巴西的准备策略。方法:我们使用 2019 年至 2023 年间通过 SIVEP 系统收集的国家 监测 数据进行了一项回顾性、观察性、描述性人群研究。我们分析了由 RSV、流感和 COVID-19 引起的确诊病例、住院和死亡。我们通过局部估计散点图平滑方法使用多重季节趋势分解进行时间序列分解和季节趋势分析。我们计算了每个病因学组成部分的月平均值,以评估其季节性负担。结果:SIVEP 报告的实验室确诊严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 病例中,有 69,389 例 RSV 病例、45,881 例流感病例和 2,299,712 例 COVID-19 病例。每年,超过 90% 的 RSV 诊断发生在 0-10 岁儿童中,而流感和 COVID-19 在老年人中更为常见。与 RSV 相关的儿童死亡比例从 2020 年的 19.2% 增加到 2023 年的 62.0%。RSV 的季节性高峰出现在 3 月至 6 月,流感病例在 1 月达到高峰,而 COVID-19 的季节性高峰则不太一致。观察到地理差异,巴西东南部和南部地区病例集中度较高。结论:巴西国家 监测 系统报告的 SARI 病例中呼吸道病毒负担因病原体、年龄组、地区和季节而异,并且可能受到检测策略变化的影响。加强诊断能力和 监测 至关重要,特别是对于成人 RSV 病例,由于检测有限和诊断敏感性降低,这些病例可能漏报。季节性 疫苗接种 计划(例如针对流感的计划)仍然至关重要,并且可以通过整合新的预防措施(例如针对老年人的 RSV 疫苗接种 和保护婴儿的孕产妇免疫接种)来进一步加强。

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test for rapid detection of respiratory syncytial virus in children admitted to high-dependency care in Nepal
papers.abstract: Background Rapid respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) diagnostics are largely unavailable in low-resource settings. We compared the diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test (POCT) with standard reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in children admitted to high-dependency care. Methods We analysed data from a larger study (RSV GOLD - ICU Network study) in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons. Children aged ≥4 days and Results We analysed 124 randomly selected stored samples, of whom 70 (56.5%) tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4). All cases with false-negative POCT had low viral loads (CT value >31). The sensitivity (93.2%; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 86.0, 97.5), specificity (98.0%; 95% CI = 91.5, 99.9), positive predictive values (98.6%; 95% CI = 93.9, 99.9), and negative predictive values (90.7%; 95% CI = 81.1, 96.6) of POCT for RSV infection were all satisfactory. Conclusions We conducted the first prospective study showing excellent accuracy of molecular RSV POCT in a poor resource setting. Affordable molecular-based POCT in resource-constrained settings can improve care of children with acute respiratory infections and strengthen surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during rollout of RSV interventions.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons, analyzing data from a larger study (RSV GOLD - ICU Network study) involving 124 randomly selected stored samples from children aged ≥4 days.
analysis.methods: The diagnostic accuracy of the molecular-based POCT was compared with standard reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) using stored samples. The study analyzed data from a larger prospective study in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons.
analysis.main_results: Of the 124 samples, 70 (56.5%) tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4). All cases with false-negative POCT had low viral loads (CT value >31).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that the molecular-based POCT has excellent accuracy for RSV detection in a resource-constrained setting, as demonstrated by its high sensitivity and specificity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that affordable molecular-based POCT can improve the care of children with acute respiratory infections and enhance surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during the rollout of RSV interventions.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test (POCT) for rapid detection of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in children admitted to high-dependency care in Nepal. The POCT was compared with standard RT-PCR using 124 stored samples. Results showed that 70 (56.5%) samples tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4), with all false-negative POCT cases having low viral loads (CT value >31). The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating excellent accuracy of the POCT for RSV detection in a resource-constrained setting, with high sensitivity (93.2%) and specificity (98.0%). These results suggest that affordable molecular-based POCT could improve care for children with acute respiratory infections and strengthen surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during RSV intervention rollouts. The study is limited by its use of stored samples and analysis based on a single respiratory season, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test (POCT) for rapid detection of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in children admitted to high-dependency care in low-resource settings, where rapid diagnostics are largely unavailable.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons, analyzing data from a larger study (RSV GOLD - ICU Network study) involving 124 randomly selected stored samples from children aged ≥4 days.
elements_en.methods: The diagnostic accuracy of the molecular-based POCT was compared with standard reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) using stored samples. The study analyzed data from a larger prospective study in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons.
elements_en.main_results: Of the 124 samples, 70 (56.5%) tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4). All cases with false-negative POCT had low viral loads (CT value >31).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that the molecular-based POCT has excellent accuracy for RSV detection in a resource-constrained setting, as demonstrated by its high sensitivity and specificity.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that affordable molecular-based POCT can improve the care of children with acute respiratory infections and enhance surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during the rollout of RSV interventions.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on stored samples, which may introduce potential biases, and the analysis was based on a single respiratory season. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估基于分子的现场护理测试 (POCT) 的诊断准确性,该测试可快速检测在资源匮乏地区接受高度依赖护理的儿童中的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),而这些地区基本上无法进行快速诊断。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究在尼泊尔两家三级医院进行了两个呼吸季节,分析了一项大型研究(RSV GOLD - ICU 网络研究)的数据,该研究涉及 124 个随机选择的 4 天以上儿童的储存样本。
elements_zh.methods: 使用存储的样本将基于分子的 POCT 的诊断准确性与标准逆转录聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 进行比较。该研究分析了尼泊尔两家三级医院在两个呼吸季节进行的一项更大规模前瞻性研究的数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 124 份样本中,70 份(56.5%)经 POCT 检测呈阳性,74 份(59.7%)经 RT-PCR 检测呈阳性。中位周期阈值 (CT) 值为 29.1(四分位数范围 = 25.1-33.4)。所有 POCT 假阴性病例的病毒载量均较低(CT 值 >31)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为,基于分子的 POCT 在资源有限的环境中对 RSV 检测具有出色的准确性,正如其高灵敏度和特异性所证明的那样。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,负担得起的基于分子的 POCT 可以改善急性呼吸道感染儿童的护理,并在推出 RSV 干预措施期间增强 监测 的 疫苗 有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对存储样本的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入潜在的偏差,并且分析是基于单个呼吸季节。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 用于快速检测尼泊尔高度依赖护理儿童中 呼吸道合胞病毒 的分子护理点测试的诊断准确性
papers.source_body_en: Background Rapid respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) diagnostics are largely unavailable in low-resource settings. We compared the diagnostic accuracy of a molecular-based point-of-care test (POCT) with standard reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in children admitted to high-dependency care. Methods We analysed data from a larger study (RSV GOLD - ICU Network study) in two Nepali tertiary hospitals over two respiratory seasons. Children aged ≥4 days and Results We analysed 124 randomly selected stored samples, of whom 70 (56.5%) tested positive with POCT and 74 (59.7%) with RT-PCR. The median cycle threshold (CT) value was 29.1 (interquartile range = 25.1-33.4). All cases with false-negative POCT had low viral loads (CT value >31). The sensitivity (93.2%; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 86.0, 97.5), specificity (98.0%; 95% CI = 91.5, 99.9), positive predictive values (98.6%; 95% CI = 93.9, 99.9), and negative predictive values (90.7%; 95% CI = 81.1, 96.6) of POCT for RSV infection were all satisfactory. Conclusions We conducted the first prospective study showing excellent accuracy of molecular RSV POCT in a poor resource setting. Affordable molecular-based POCT in resource-constrained settings can improve care of children with acute respiratory infections and strengthen surveillance for vaccine effectiveness during rollout of RSV interventions.

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness in Medicare Beneficiaries Residing in Nursing Homes
papers.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates are needed to determine the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccinations during their first season of availability among populations at high risk for severe RSV. OBJECTIVE: To assess RSV VE against RSV-associated outcomes for nursing home residents. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study of Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries used electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024. A cohort was created for each outcome: an RSV-associated hospitalization cohort; an RSV-associated death cohort; a severe RSV-associated outcome cohort; and an RSV-associated thromboembolic event cohort. To be eligible for inclusion in a cohort, a Medicare fee-for-service beneficiary must be aged 65 years or older, reside in a US nursing home during the study period for at least 1 day, have continuous enrollment in Medicare Parts A and B (365 days prior to the index date), and have continuous enrollment in Part D (beginning on June 21, 2023). EXPOSURE: RSV vaccination. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Outcomes were RSV-associated hospitalization, RSV-associated death, severe RSV-associated outcomes (intensive care unit or critical care unit admission, medical ventilator use, or RSV-associated death), and RSV-associated thromboembolic event. RSV diagnoses and outcome definitions were based on claims with relevant International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes. RSV vaccine doses were determined from Medicare Part D claims using the National Drug Code Directory. Hazard ratios (HRs) from multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared the times to first outcomes among RSV vaccinated beneficiaries and unvaccinated beneficiaries. VE was calculated as (1-HR) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 597 430 included Medicare beneficiaries (66% female; median age, 82 [IQR, 75-88] years), RSV VE against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%). Among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years VE was 60% (95% CI, 35%-76%), 75% (95% CI, 67%-82%) among beneficiaries 75 years or older, 67% (95% CI, 55%-76%) among short-stay residents (<100 cumulative days), and 80% (95% CI, 68%-87%) among long-stay residents (≥100 cumulative days). VE against RSV-associated death was 56% (95% CI, 39%-69%), VE against severe RSV-associated outcomes was 59% (95% CI, 44%-70%), and VE against RSV-associated thromboembolic events was 66% (95% CI, 44%-79%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, in the first season of availability, RSV vaccines were associated with improved RSV-associated outcomes among US Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines among Medicare beneficiaries residing in nursing homes during their first season of availability. Using electronic medical claims data from September 10, 2023, to March 30, 2024, the researchers created cohorts based on RSV-associated outcomes, including hospitalization, death, severe outcomes, and thromboembolic events. They found that vaccine effectiveness (VE) against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 73% (95% CI, 65%-79%), with varying effectiveness across age groups and residency duration. VE against RSV-associated death was 56%, against severe outcomes was 59%, and against thromboembolic events was 66%. The study highlights the potential benefits of RSV vaccination in high-risk populations but notes limitations due to the observational nature of the data and possible confounding factors. These findings may inform future public health strategies for RSV prevention in nursing home settings.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项研究中,在可用的第一个季节,RSV 疫苗 与居住在疗养院的美国医疗保险受益人的 RSV 相关结果改善相关。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这项研究中,在可用的第一个季节,RSV 疫苗 与居住在疗养院的美国医疗保险受益人的 RSV 相关结果改善相关。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为 监测 和疗养院居民等高危人群中 RSV 的风险评估策略提供信息,并可能指导未来 疫苗 在此人群中有效性的研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于索赔数据,这可能会引入偏差或混杂因素,并且结果的普遍性可能仅限于疗养院的医疗保险受益人。由于依赖观察数据和潜在的无法测量的混杂因素,证据是中等的。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Symptomatic Fraction, Shedding and Detection in Children Aged 6–23 Months in South Africa in 2022
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Accurate detection of RSV infections is important to understand epidemiology. We estimated symptomatic fraction and shedding duration of reverse‐transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT‐PCR)‐confirmed cases and compared RSV detection through molecular and serologic techniques. Methods We enrolled healthy children aged 6–23 months in a prospective cohort study, from May to October 2022, collecting thrice‐weekly mid‐turbinate nasal swabs for RSV RT‐PCR testing. We collected serum at baseline and end of follow‐up and detected anti‐RSV IgG using enzyme‐linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and multipathogen bead‐based immunoassay (MIA). We ascertained symptoms by twice‐weekly nurse visits, and daily caregiver symptom diaries. We calculated sensitivity, specificity, and positive (PPV) and negative (NPV) predictive value of RT‐PCR, ELISA, and MIA compared to a standard (two or more assays‐positive) among children with paired sera and baseline blood preceding an RT‐PCR–confirmed episode. Results The RSV season started mid‐February 2022. We enrolled 93 participants; 87 (94%) followed to the final study visit. Forty individuals had one or more RT‐PCR–confirmed RSV infection, and six of them had a repeat episode. One‐or‐more symptom was reported from 54% (25/46) of RT‐PCR–confirmed episodes, fever in 26% (12/46), and cough in 37% (17/46). Median RNA shedding duration was 7 days (IQR = 4–11 days). Among 80 children meeting criteria, ELISA and MIA each had > 92% sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV while RT‐PCR had 78% (95% CI = 61%–90%) sensitivity, 98% (95% CI = 88–100%) specificity, 97% (95% CI = 82%–100%) PPV, and 84% (95% CI = 71%–93%) NPV. Discussion Approximately half of RSV episodes were symptomatic. Serology had a high sensitivity and specificity for infection identification.

papers.title: Hospital Admissions for Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Among Elderly: A Retrospective Study From an Italian Southern Region During Years 2018–2023
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is one of the most common causes of acute respiratory infections in both children and adults over 60. RSV can cause severe lower respiratory tract infections in older adults, leading to an increase of morbidity and mortality. The aim of this study was to assess the incidence of hospitalizations due to RSV infections in the Abruzzo region of Italy among patients aged over 60 years. Methods A retrospective study was performed in the Abruzzo region, evaluating all hospitalizations performed during years 2018–2023. Age‐ and gender‐standardized hospitalization rates for RSV were calculated. Patients' comorbidities and hospitalization‐related outcomes were also assessed. Results During 2018–2023, 42 RSV‐coded hospitalizations were identified among adults aged ≥ 60 years. An additional RSV‐attributable burden was estimated by applying a literature‐derived attributable fraction to hospitalizations for unspecified viral bronchiolitis and pneumonia, resulting in an estimated total of 67 RSV‐attributable admissions. Annual age‐ and sex‐standardized RSV‐coded hospitalization rates showed substantial year‐to‐year variability. Poisson regression with correction for overdispersion identified no statistically significant temporal trend during the study period (IRR per calendar year 1.08, 95% CI 0.86–1.34; p = 0.516). Among patients with RSV‐coded admissions, the median length of stay was 11 days (IQR 6–18), and four patients (9.52%) died during hospitalization. Conclusions RSV was associated with a measurable burden of hospitalization among older adults in Abruzzo. However, substantial year‐to‐year variability and the small number of RSV‐coded admissions warrant cautious interpretation of temporal patterns. No statistically significant temporal trend was identified during the study period.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是儿童和 60 岁以上成人急性呼吸道感染的最常见原因之一。RSV 可引起老年人严重的下呼吸道感染,导致发病率和 死亡率 增加。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在阿布鲁佐地区进行了一项回顾性研究,评估了 2018 年至 2023 年期间的所有住院治疗情况。本研究的目的是评估意大利阿布鲁佐地区 60 岁以上患者因 RSV 感染住院的 发病率。
elements_zh.methods: Age‐ and gender‐standardized hospitalization rates for RSV were calculated. Poisson regression with correction for overdispersion identified no statistically significant temporal trend during the study period (IRR per calendar year 1.08, 95% CI 0.86–1.34; p = 0.516).
elements_zh.main_results: 2018 年至 2023 年期间,在 60 岁以上的成年人中发现了 42 例 RSV 编码住院病例。年年龄和性别标准化 RSV 编码住院率显示出显着的逐年变化。在RSV编码入院的患者中,中位住院时间为11天(IQR 6-18),四名患者(9.52%)在住院期间死亡。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RSV 与阿布鲁佐老年人的可衡量的住院负担相关。然而,每年的巨大差异和 RSV 编码的入院人数较少,需要对时间模式进行谨慎的解释。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RSV 给老年人群带来了显着的住院负担,凸显了针对这一人群进行针对性 监测 和干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计依赖于回顾性数据,并且 RSV 编码的入院人数较少,限制了观察到的时间趋势的可信度。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

papers.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes and Acute Human Metapneumovirus Infection in Adults: A Systematic Literature Review.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory viral infections, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, are well-recognized as being associated with cardiovascular events (CVEs). In contrast, the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the prevalence of pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the incidence of acute CVEs in adults with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. METHODS: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (Jan.-2000/Sept.-2025). Observational studies and clinical trials reporting pre-existing CVDs and/or CVEs in adults (≥18 years) were included. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which nine underwent critical appraisal. Most involved hospitalized older adults. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10%-80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common conditions. Acute CVEs, particularly heart failure exacerbations, occurred in 5%-25% of hospitalized patients. Underlying CVD was consistently linked to increased severity of HMPV illness, including higher rates of ICU admission and mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Acute HMPV infection frequently occurs in adults with pre-existing CVD and may be associated with CVEs in older hospitalized populations. However, evidence remains limited and largely observational. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the potential CV complications associated with HMPV infection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO [CRD420251164583].

papers.title_zh: 成人心血管结局和急性人间质肺病毒感染:系统文献综述。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Acute respiratory viral infections, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, are well-recognized as being associated with cardiovascular events (CVEs). In contrast, the cardiovascular impact of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) remains poorly characterized. We aimed to describe the prevalence of pre-existing cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the incidence of acute CVEs in adults with laboratory-confirmed HMPV infection. METHODS: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Google Scholar (Jan.-2000/Sept.-2025). Observational studies and clinical trials reporting pre-existing CVDs and/or CVEs in adults (≥18 years) were included. RESULTS: Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria, of which nine underwent critical appraisal. Most involved hospitalized older adults. Pre-existing CVD was reported in 10%-80% of HMPV-infected patients, with chronic heart failure and coronary artery disease being the most common conditions. Acute CVEs, particularly heart failure exacerbations, occurred in 5%-25% of hospitalized patients. Underlying CVD was consistently linked to increased severity of HMPV illness, including higher rates of ICU admission and mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Acute HMPV infection frequently occurs in adults with pre-existing CVD and may be associated with CVEs in older hospitalized populations. However, evidence remains limited and largely observational. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the potential CV complications associated with HMPV infection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: PROSPERO [CRD420251164583].

papers.title: Comparative effectiveness of preventive strategies against medically-attended respiratory syncytial virus in U.S. infants during the first six months of life, 2023-2025
papers.abstract: Importance: Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies are now available in the U.S. Long-acting monoclonal antibody administration in the U.S. commonly occurs after hospital discharge in outpatient settings, leaving some infants unprotected early in life when severe RSV risk is highest. Comparative effectiveness between the two interventions and whether delays affect effectiveness estimates have not been quantified. Objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of infant long-acting monoclonal antibody strategies and a maternal vaccination strategy, each compared to no intervention, and the comparative effectiveness of intervention strategies when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt. Design: Cohort study using target trial emulation to compare four strategies for prevention of RSV-related outcomes. between 2023 and 2025 using a nationwide database of employer-sponsored commercial insurance claims. Participants: 120,586 commercially insured mother-infants, whose infants were born in the U.S. during the 2023-2024 or 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants who could not be paired with their mother's record, did not enroll in commercial insurance within 75 days from birth, received palivizumab, and had an implausible birth date were excluded. Interventions: Comparison of four RSV prevention strategies: (i) maternal RSVpreF; (ii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within the first week of life (mAb as intended); (iii) long-acting monoclonal antibody given within a six-month grace period from birth (mAb within grace period); and (iv) a control. Main outcomes and measures: Effectiveness against first RSV-associated hospitalization and medically-attended RSV illness was summarized using adjusted hazard ratios (aHR) and estimated using an inverse propensity weighting approach, with weights accounting for maternal age, maternal comorbidities affecting pregnancy, obstetric and newborn complications, season, region, and birth timing relative to October 1. A weighted Kaplan Meier estimator was used to estimate strategy-specific cumulative incidence of RSV outcomes over time. Results: In the first five weeks of life, the mAb within grace period strategy doubled the hazard of RSV hospitalization (aHR: 2.0 [95% CI: 1.0-4.9]) and increased the hazard of medically-attended RSV (aHR: 1.6 [95% CI: 1.0-2.7]) compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy. The hazard for RSV hospitalization was similar for the mAb as intended strategy compared to the maternal RSVpreF strategy (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9]). Conclusions and relevance: RSVpreF and monoclonal antibodies were similarly effective when monoclonal antibodies were administered close to birth, but when accounting for real-world delays in monoclonal antibody receipt, the maternal RSVpreF strategy was more effective than the mAb within grace period strategy.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the effectiveness of maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies in preventing RSV-related outcomes in U.S. infants during the first six months of life. It compares four strategies: maternal RSVpreF, monoclonal antibody given within the first week of life, monoclonal antibody given within a six-month grace period, and a control. The study uses a nationwide database of commercial insurance claims and employs adjusted hazard ratios and inverse propensity weighting to account for confounding factors. Results show that the mAb within grace period strategy had a higher hazard of RSV hospitalization and medically-attended RSV compared to maternal RSVpreF in the first five weeks of life, while the mAb as intended strategy was similarly effective to maternal RSVpreF. The authors conclude that maternal RSVpreF is more effective when considering real-world delays in monoclonal antibody administration. The study's findings have implications for public health strategies, emphasizing the importance of timely intervention. However, the study's reliance on insurance data and observational design limits the strength of the evidence.

papers.abstract_zh: 重要性:母体 疫苗接种 和长效单克隆抗体现已在美国上市。在美国,长效单克隆抗体给药通常发生在出院后的门诊环境中,导致一些婴儿在生命早期严重 RSV 风险最高时得不到保护。两种干预措施之间的有效性比较以及延迟是否影响有效性估计尚未得到量化。目的:评估婴儿长效单克隆抗体策略和母亲 疫苗接种 策略的有效性,分别与无干预进行比较,以及在考虑单克隆抗体接收的实际延迟时干预策略的比较有效性。设计:队列研究 研究使用目标试验模拟来比较四种预防 RSV 相关结果的策略。2023 年至 2025 年间,使用全国范围内雇主资助的商业保险索赔数据库。参与者:120,586 名有商业保险的母婴,其婴儿在 2023-2024 年或 2024-2025 年 RSV 季节期间在美国出生。无法与母亲记录配对、出生后75天内未参加商业保险、接受帕利珠单抗治疗以及出生日期不可信的婴儿被排除在外。干预措施:四种 RSV 预防策略的比较:(i) 母体 RSVpreF;(ii) 在出生后第一周内给予长效单克隆抗体(按预期使用单克隆抗体);(iii) 在出生后六个月的宽限期内给予长效单克隆抗体(宽限期内的单克隆抗体);(iv) 对照。主要结果和措施:使用调整后的风险比(aHR)总结了针对首次 RSV 相关住院和就医 RSV 疾病的有效性,并使用逆倾向加权方法进行了估计,权重考虑了产妇年龄、影响妊娠的孕产妇合并症、产科和新生儿并发症、季节、地区和相对于 10 月 1 日的出生时间。使用加权 Kaplan Meier 估计器来估计 RSV 结果的特定策略累积 发病率时间。结果:在出生后的前五周,与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,宽限期内使用 mAb 策略使 RSV 住院风险加倍(aHR:2.0 [95% CI:1.0-4.9]),并增加就医 RSV 风险(aHR:1.6 [95% CI:1.0-2.7])。与母体 RSVpreF 策略相比,mAb 预期策略的 RSV 住院风险相似 (aHR = 0.9 [95% CI: 0.3-1.9])。结论和相关性:当临近出生时施用单克隆抗体时,RSVpreF 和单克隆抗体的效果相似,但考虑到单克隆抗体接收的实际延迟时,母体 RSVpreF 策略比宽限期内的 mAb 策略更有效。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
papers.abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

papers.title: Impact of respiratory syncytial virus immunization in older adults: the importance of a valid burden estimation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction In the province of Québec, Canada, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization program restricted to seniors residing in long-term care facilities (LTCF) and those aged ≥75 years from private senior residences (PSR) was implemented in Fall 2024, with approximately 65% vaccine uptake in the targeted populations. Despite high vaccine effectiveness, the real-world impact of the RSV immunization program on population-level averted hospitalizations and the influence that RSV diagnostic test performance might have remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of the first season (2024-25) of the intervention among older adults in Québec while accounting for laboratory test performance. Methods A prospective hospital-based surveillance (HospiVir) and health administrative databases were used to assess the intervention impact. Observed to expected approach and before/after ecological design using a difference-in-difference Poisson regression, both accounting for seasonal variations and trends in comparison groups, were used. Hospitalization incidence rate estimates based on hospital-based surveillance were adjusted for the laboratory test performances using Lash equations. Results Based on HospiVir, a 49% (95% confidence interval (CI): -80– -5) decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations was observed among adults aged ≥75 years residing in PSR. This decrease was 23% (95% CI: -38–66) in the overall population ≥75 years. A smaller decrease for the overall population ≥75 years was observed using health administrative data, but it did not reach statistical significance (10%; 95% CI: -7–23). The impact of the immunization program did not change following adjustment for diagnostic test performance, while the absolute burden of RSV-associated hospitalizations varied according to the proportion of RSV test positivity. Conclusions The 2024-25 RSV immunization program was associated with an almost 50% reduction in hospitalizations in residents of PSR aged ≥75 years. The magnitude of this reduction was roughly twofold lower when considering the overall population aged ≥75 years. Expanding the target population and strengthening vaccine promotion efforts to improve uptake are both essential to enhance the population-level impact of the RSV immunization program.

papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Introduction In the province of Québec, Canada, a respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization program restricted to seniors residing in long-term care facilities (LTCF) and those aged ≥75 years from private senior residences (PSR) was implemented in Fall 2024, with approximately 65% vaccine uptake in the targeted populations. Despite high vaccine effectiveness, the real-world impact of the RSV immunization program on population-level averted hospitalizations and the influence that RSV diagnostic test performance might have remains unknown. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of the first season (2024-25) of the intervention among older adults in Québec while accounting for laboratory test performance. Methods A prospective hospital-based surveillance (HospiVir) and health administrative databases were used to assess the intervention impact. Observed to expected approach and before/after ecological design using a difference-in-difference Poisson regression, both accounting for seasonal variations and trends in comparison groups, were used. Hospitalization incidence rate estimates based on hospital-based surveillance were adjusted for the laboratory test performances using Lash equations. Results Based on HospiVir, a 49% (95% confidence interval (CI): -80– -5) decrease in RSV-associated hospitalizations was observed among adults aged ≥75 years residing in PSR. This decrease was 23% (95% CI: -38–66) in the overall population ≥75 years. A smaller decrease for the overall population ≥75 years was observed using health administrative data, but it did not reach statistical significance (10%; 95% CI: -7–23). The impact of the immunization program did not change following adjustment for diagnostic test performance, while the absolute burden of RSV-associated hospitalizations varied according to the proportion of RSV test positivity. Conclusions The 2024-25 RSV immunization program was associated with an almost 50% reduction in hospitalizations in residents of PSR aged ≥75 years. The magnitude of this reduction was roughly twofold lower when considering the overall population aged ≥75 years. Expanding the target population and strengthening vaccine promotion efforts to improve uptake are both essential to enhance the population-level impact of the RSV immunization program.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 简介 加拿大魁北克省于 2024 年秋季实施了一项 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 免疫计划,仅限于长期护理机构 (LTCF) 中的老年人和私人老年住宅 (PSR) 中年龄≥75 岁的老年人,目标人群中 疫苗 的接种率约为 65%。尽管 疫苗 的有效性很高,但 RSV 免疫计划对人群避免住院治疗的实际影响以及 RSV 诊断测试性能可能产生的影响仍然未知。本研究旨在评估第一季(2024-25 年)干预措施对魁北克老年人的影响,同时考虑实验室测试表现。方法 使用基于医院的前瞻性 监测 (HospiVir) 和健康管理数据库来评估干预效果。使用双差泊松回归对预期方法和生态设计之前/之后进行观察,同时考虑了季节变化和比较组中的趋势。基于医院 发病率 的住院 发病率 率估计值使用 Lash 方程根据实验室测试表现进行了调整。结果 根据 HospiVir,居住在 PSR 的 75 岁以上成年人中,观察到与 RSV 相关的住院治疗减少了 49%(95% 置信区间 (CI):-80–-5)。在 75 岁以上的总体人群中,这一下降幅度为 23% (95% CI: -38–66)。使用卫生管理数据观察到,≥75 岁的总人口下降幅度较小,但未达到统计显着性(10%;95% CI:-7-23)。免疫接种计划的影响在诊断测试表现调整后没有变化,而 RSV 相关住院的绝对负担根据 RSV 测试阳性的比例而变化。结论 2024-25 RSV 免疫计划与 PSR 年龄≥75 岁居民的住院率减少近 50% 相关。考虑到 75 岁以上的总人口,这一减少幅度大约低两倍。扩大目标人群和加强 疫苗 推广工作以提高接种率对于增强 RSV 免疫计划在人群层面的影响至关重要。

papers.title: Extreme weather and high-level PM2.5 co-exposure are associated with elevated respiratory syncytial virus circulating intensity
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Higher temperatures and more frequent heat waves and cold spells due to climate change raise concerns for respiratory health. However, the association of extreme temperature events with RSV epidemics remains unclear. Method We conducted time-series analyses to assess relative risks from exposure to extreme temperatures alone and joint exposure to extreme temperatures and high-level particulate matter [2.5 microns or less in diameter ( $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 )] pollution on RSV circulating strength. Japan and Chile were selected as two contrasting settings with distinct climatic and geographic backgrounds. Weekly data on laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases, denominator population, meteorological factors, and air pollutants were collected from 16 Chilean regions (2015–2018) and 47 Japanese prefectures (2013–2019). We fitted quasi-Poisson regression to assess the local-level estimates and used random-effects meta-analyses to obtain national estimates. Results Here we show that heat waves are linked to increased RSV circulating intensity in Japan, with relative risks up to 1.49 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–1.73). Cold spells show weaker but positive effects. Although cold spells demonstrate no consistent effects in Chile, joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and cold spells increases risks by 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58). Joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and heat waves raises risk by up to 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16) in Japan. Conclusions These findings reveal national patterns and regional variations in RSV responses to extreme temperatures, highlighting the need for public health measures targeting modifiable population-level factors amid global climate change.

papers.title_original: Extreme weather and high-level PM2.5 co-exposure are associated with elevated respiratory syncytial virus circulating intensity

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unclear association between extreme temperature events and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) epidemics amid rising concerns for respiratory health due to climate change. It aimed to quantify how extreme temperatures, alone or combined with high-level PM2.5 pollution, influence RSV circulating intensity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted time-series analyses using weekly data from 16 Chilean regions (2015–2018) and 47 Japanese prefectures (2013–2019). It assessed RSV circulating strength in relation to meteorological factors and air pollutants, focusing on extreme temperature events and PM2.5 exposure.
analysis.methods: Quasi-Poisson regression models were fitted to estimate local-level relative risks of RSV cases associated with extreme temperatures and high-level PM2.5 pollution. Random-effects meta-analyses were then used to derive national-level estimates from the local data.
analysis.main_results: Heat waves were linked to increased RSV circulating intensity in Japan, with relative risks up to 1.49 (95% CI: 1.29–1.73). Joint exposure to high-level PM2.5 and heat waves raised risk by up to 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16) in Japan, while joint exposure to PM2.5 and cold spells increased risks by 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58). Cold spells showed weaker but positive effects.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal national patterns and regional variations in RSV responses to extreme temperatures, highlighting modifiable population-level factors that may influence RSV transmission under climate change. This is the first study to quantify joint effects of extreme temperatures and PM2.5 on RSV circulating intensity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that public health measures targeting extreme temperature events and air pollution could mitigate RSV burden, particularly in regions with high PM2.5 levels and frequent heat waves or cold spells.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design, which precludes causal inference and may be affected by unmeasured confounders such as healthcare-seeking behavior and testing practices. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on aggregated data and absence of individual-level controls.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between extreme temperature events and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) circulating intensity, addressing a critical knowledge gap amid climate change concerns. Using time-series analyses of weekly RSV case data from Japan and Chile, the authors quantified the relative risks of RSV cases linked to heat waves, cold spells, and joint exposure to high-level PM2.5 pollution. Heat waves were associated with increased RSV intensity in Japan (RR up to 1.49), while joint exposure to PM2.5 and extreme temperatures further elevated risks (up to 66% for heat waves and 32% for cold spells). Cold spells showed weaker but positive effects. The findings highlight regional variations in RSV responses and underscore the potential for public health interventions targeting extreme temperatures and air pollution to reduce RSV burden under changing climate conditions.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unclear association between extreme temperature events and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) epidemics amid rising concerns for respiratory health due to climate change. It aimed to quantify how extreme temperatures, alone or combined with high-level PM2.5 pollution, influence RSV circulating intensity.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study conducted time-series analyses using weekly data from 16 Chilean regions (2015–2018) and 47 Japanese prefectures (2013–2019). It assessed RSV circulating strength in relation to meteorological factors and air pollutants, focusing on extreme temperature events and PM2.5 exposure.
elements_en.methods: Quasi-Poisson regression models were fitted to estimate local-level relative risks of RSV cases associated with extreme temperatures and high-level PM2.5 pollution. Random-effects meta-analyses were then used to derive national-level estimates from the local data.
elements_en.main_results: Heat waves were linked to increased RSV circulating intensity in Japan, with relative risks up to 1.49 (95% CI: 1.29–1.73). Joint exposure to high-level PM2.5 and heat waves raised risk by up to 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16) in Japan, while joint exposure to PM2.5 and cold spells increased risks by 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58). Cold spells showed weaker but positive effects.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings reveal national patterns and regional variations in RSV responses to extreme temperatures, highlighting modifiable population-level factors that may influence RSV transmission under climate change. This is the first study to quantify joint effects of extreme temperatures and PM2.5 on RSV circulating intensity.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that public health measures targeting extreme temperature events and air pollution could mitigate RSV burden, particularly in regions with high PM2.5 levels and frequent heat waves or cold spells.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its ecological design, which precludes causal inference and may be affected by unmeasured confounders such as healthcare-seeking behavior and testing practices. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on aggregated data and absence of individual-level controls.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于气候变化,人们对呼吸系统健康的担忧日益加剧,该研究解决了极端温度事件与 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 流行病之间尚不清楚的关联问题。其目的是量化极端温度(单独或与高浓度 PM2.5 污染结合)如何影响 RSV 循环强度。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用智利 16 个地区(2015-2018 年)和日本 47 个都道府县(2013-2019 年)的每周数据进行时间序列分析。它评估了 RSV 循环强度与气象因素和空气污染物的关系,重点关注极端温度事件和 PM2.5 暴露。
elements_zh.methods: 拟合准泊松回归模型来估计与极端温度和高浓度 PM2.5 污染相关的当地 RSV 病例相对风险。然后使用随机效应荟萃分析从当地数据得出国家层面的估计。
elements_zh.main_results: 热浪与日本 RSV 循环强度增加有关,相对风险高达 1.49(95% CI:1.29-1.73)。在日本,同时暴露于高浓度 PM2.5 和热浪会使风险增加高达 66%(95% CI:1.27–2.16),而同时暴露于 PM2.5 和寒流会使风险增加 32%(95% CI:1.10–1.58)。寒潮表现出较弱但积极的影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果揭示了 RSV 对极端温度反应的国家模式和区域差异,强调了在气候变化下可能影响 RSV 传播 的可改变的种群水平因素。这是第一项量化极端温度和 PM2.5 对 RSV 循环强度联合影响的研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果表明,针对极端温度事件和空气污染的公共卫生措施可以减轻 RSV 负担,特别是在 PM2.5 水平较高且热浪或寒流频繁的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到其生态设计的限制,无法进行因果推断,并且可能受到未测量的混杂因素(例如就医行为和测试实践)的影响。由于依赖汇总数据且缺乏个体层面的控制,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 极端天气和高浓度 PM2.5 共同暴露与 呼吸道合胞病毒 循环强度升高有关
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Higher temperatures and more frequent heat waves and cold spells due to climate change raise concerns for respiratory health. However, the association of extreme temperature events with RSV epidemics remains unclear. Method We conducted time-series analyses to assess relative risks from exposure to extreme temperatures alone and joint exposure to extreme temperatures and high-level particulate matter [2.5 microns or less in diameter ( $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 )] pollution on RSV circulating strength. Japan and Chile were selected as two contrasting settings with distinct climatic and geographic backgrounds. Weekly data on laboratory-confirmed RSV-positive cases, denominator population, meteorological factors, and air pollutants were collected from 16 Chilean regions (2015–2018) and 47 Japanese prefectures (2013–2019). We fitted quasi-Poisson regression to assess the local-level estimates and used random-effects meta-analyses to obtain national estimates. Results Here we show that heat waves are linked to increased RSV circulating intensity in Japan, with relative risks up to 1.49 (95% confidence interval (CI): 1.29–1.73). Cold spells show weaker but positive effects. Although cold spells demonstrate no consistent effects in Chile, joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and cold spells increases risks by 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58). Joint exposure to high-level $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 pollution and heat waves raises risk by up to 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16) in Japan. Conclusions These findings reveal national patterns and regional variations in RSV responses to extreme temperatures, highlighting the need for public health measures targeting modifiable population-level factors amid global climate change.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 气候变化导致气温升高、热浪和寒潮更加频繁,引起了人们对呼吸系统健康的担忧。然而,极端温度事件与 RSV 流行之间的关联仍不清楚。方法 我们进行了时间序列分析,以评估单独暴露于极端温度以及联合暴露于极端温度和高浓度颗粒物 [直径 2.5 微米或更小 ( $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 )] 污染对 RSV 循环强度的相对风险。日本和智利被选为两个气候和地理背景截然不同的国家。从智利 16 个地区(2015-2018 年)和日本 47 个都道府县(2013-2019 年)收集了有关实验室确诊 RSV 阳性病例、分母人口、气象因素和空气污染物的每周数据。我们拟合准泊松回归来评估当地水平的估计值,并使用随机效应荟萃分析来获得国家估计值。结果 我们在此表明​​,热浪与日本 RSV 循环强度增加有关,相对风险高达 1.49(95% 置信区间 (CI):1.29–1.73)。寒潮表现出较弱但积极的影响。尽管寒潮在智利没有表现出一致的影响,但同时暴露于高浓度 $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 污染和寒潮会使风险增加 32% (95% CI: 1.10–1.58)。在日本,同时暴露于高浓度 $${{{\rm{PM}}}}_{2.5}$$ PM 2.5 污染和热浪会使风险增加高达 66% (95% CI: 1.27–2.16)。结论 这些发现揭示了 RSV 对极端温度反应的国家模式和区域差异,强调了在全球气候变化中针对可改变的人口水平因素采取公共卫生措施的必要性。

papers.title: Changes in respiratory virus seasonality across the COVID-19 pandemic: a multicentre comparative study in Leicester, Rotterdam, Hong Kong, and Christchurch.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe respiratory virus seasonality before, during, and after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) using routine hospital diagnostic laboratory data contributed through the International Network for the Sequencing of Respiratory Viruses (INSPIRE). METHODS: We analysed monthly test data from four diagnostic laboratories in Leicester, UK; Rotterdam, the Netherlands; Hong Kong, China; and Christchurch, New Zealand, during 2018-2023. Viruses included influenza A virus, influenza B virus, respiratory syncytial virus, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus, and enterovirus/rhinovirus. Monthly test positivity was compared across pre-COVID-19 (2018-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 re-emergence (2022-2023) periods. RESULTS: The dataset comprised 3,164,720 tests performed and 84,300 positive detections. During 2020-2021, influenza activity was markedly suppressed: influenza A virus positivity decreased from 7.3% to 1.2%, and influenza B virus positivity from 3.0% to 0.1%. Respiratory syncytial virus showed a smaller overall reduction, whereas enterovirus/rhinovirus remained detectable in all four sites. In 2022-2023, respiratory viruses re-emerged heterogeneously; peak months differed by at least two months between the pre- and post-COVID-19 periods in 21 of 40 site-virus combinations. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory virus seasonality was substantially altered during and after COVID-19. Post-COVID-19 re-emergence varied by virus and site, supporting continued multi-pathogen surveillance.

papers.title_zh: COVID-19 大流行期间呼吸道病毒季节性的变化:莱斯特、鹿特丹、香港和基督城的多中心比较研究。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: To describe respiratory virus seasonality before, during, and after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) using routine hospital diagnostic laboratory data contributed through the International Network for the Sequencing of Respiratory Viruses (INSPIRE). METHODS: We analysed monthly test data from four diagnostic laboratories in Leicester, UK; Rotterdam, the Netherlands; Hong Kong, China; and Christchurch, New Zealand, during 2018-2023. Viruses included influenza A virus, influenza B virus, respiratory syncytial virus, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, adenovirus, and enterovirus/rhinovirus. Monthly test positivity was compared across pre-COVID-19 (2018-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 re-emergence (2022-2023) periods. RESULTS: The dataset comprised 3,164,720 tests performed and 84,300 positive detections. During 2020-2021, influenza activity was markedly suppressed: influenza A virus positivity decreased from 7.3% to 1.2%, and influenza B virus positivity from 3.0% to 0.1%. Respiratory syncytial virus showed a smaller overall reduction, whereas enterovirus/rhinovirus remained detectable in all four sites. In 2022-2023, respiratory viruses re-emerged heterogeneously; peak months differed by at least two months between the pre- and post-COVID-19 periods in 21 of 40 site-virus combinations. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory virus seasonality was substantially altered during and after COVID-19. Post-COVID-19 re-emergence varied by virus and site, supporting continued multi-pathogen surveillance.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的:使用国际呼吸道病毒测序网络 (INSPIRE) 提供的常规医院诊断实验室数据来描述 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 之前、期间和之后的呼吸道病毒季节性。方法:我们分析了英国莱斯特四个诊断实验室的每月测试数据;荷兰鹿特丹;中国香港;以及 2018-2023 年期间新西兰基督城。病毒包括甲型流感病毒、乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒、副流感病毒1-4、人类偏肺病毒、腺病毒和肠道病毒/鼻病毒。对 COVID-19 之前(2018-2019 年)、COVID-19 中断(2020-2021 年)和 COVID-19 重新出现后(2022-2023 年)期间的每月测试阳性率进行了比较。结果:数据集包含 3,164,720 项测试和 84,300 项阳性检测。2020-2021年,流感活动明显受到抑制:甲型流感病毒阳性率从7.3%下降到1.2%,乙型流感病毒阳性率从3.0%下降到0.1%。呼吸道合胞病毒 总体减少幅度较小,而肠道病毒/鼻病毒在所有四个位点仍可检测到。2022-2023年,呼吸道病毒异质性重新出现;在 40 个站点病毒组合中,有 21 个在 COVID-19 之前和之后的高峰月份之间至少相差两个月。结论:在 COVID-19 期间和之后,呼吸道病毒的季节性发生了显着变化。COVID-19 后的重新出现因病毒和部位而异,支持持续的多病原体 监测。

papers.title: Clinical and Analytical Validation of a Novel Switching RT-qPCR Assay for the Simultaneous Detection of Seven Respiratory Viruses.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory viruses is essential for effective clinical management and infection control. However, conventional RT-qPCR methods are time-consuming and require complex workflows. To address these limitations, we developed a novel Switching RT-qPCR assay designed for multiplex detection of respiratory viruses with enhanced efficiency and sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of the switching RT-qPCR assay in the detection of seven major respiratory viruses: Influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, adenovirus (AdV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2). Nasopharyngeal swab specimens (n = 808) were collected from patients with respiratory symptoms. RNA was extracted and tested using both a Switching RT-qPCR assay and commercial multiplex RT-qPCR method (Allplex Respiratory Panels and Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay). The concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and analytical performances of the two methods were compared. The Switching RT-qPCR assay demonstrated a clinical sensitivity of 93.6% and a specificity of 100%, with an overall concordance rate exceeding 96%, compared with the conventional assay. Analytical sensitivity was comparable or superior across most viral targets, particularly RSV A, AdV, and hMPV. The duplex assay format enabled the efficient simultaneous detection of two targets per reaction, reducing the overall testing time while maintaining analytical accuracy. This Switching RT-qPCR assay offers a reliable, rapid, and efficient alternative for respiratory virus detection. Its simplified duplex format and high concordance with standard molecular diagnostics indicate its potential utility in routine clinical laboratories.

papers.title_zh: 用于同时检测七种呼吸道病毒的新型转换 RT-qPCR 测定的临床和分析验证。
papers.source_body_en: Rapid and accurate identification of respiratory viruses is essential for effective clinical management and infection control. However, conventional RT-qPCR methods are time-consuming and require complex workflows. To address these limitations, we developed a novel Switching RT-qPCR assay designed for multiplex detection of respiratory viruses with enhanced efficiency and sensitivity. This study aimed to evaluate the analytical and clinical performance of the switching RT-qPCR assay in the detection of seven major respiratory viruses: Influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, adenovirus (AdV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and SARS-CoV-2 (Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2). Nasopharyngeal swab specimens (n = 808) were collected from patients with respiratory symptoms. RNA was extracted and tested using both a Switching RT-qPCR assay and commercial multiplex RT-qPCR method (Allplex Respiratory Panels and Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay). The concordance, sensitivity, specificity, and analytical performances of the two methods were compared. The Switching RT-qPCR assay demonstrated a clinical sensitivity of 93.6% and a specificity of 100%, with an overall concordance rate exceeding 96%, compared with the conventional assay. Analytical sensitivity was comparable or superior across most viral targets, particularly RSV A, AdV, and hMPV. The duplex assay format enabled the efficient simultaneous detection of two targets per reaction, reducing the overall testing time while maintaining analytical accuracy. This Switching RT-qPCR assay offers a reliable, rapid, and efficient alternative for respiratory virus detection. Its simplified duplex format and high concordance with standard molecular diagnostics indicate its potential utility in routine clinical laboratories.
papers.abstract_zh: 快速、准确地识别呼吸道病毒对于有效的临床管理和感染控制至关重要。然而,传统的 RT-qPCR 方法非常耗时且需要复杂的工作流程。为了解决这些限制,我们开发了一种新型开关 RT-qPCR 检测方法,旨在提高呼吸道病毒的多重检测效率和灵敏度。本研究旨在评估转换 RT-qPCR 检测在检测七种主要呼吸道病毒时的分析和临床性能:甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A 和 B、腺病毒 (AdV)、人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 和 SARS-CoV-2(严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2)。鼻咽拭子标本(n = 808)是从有呼吸道症状的患者身上采集的。使用 Switching RT-qPCR 测定和商业多重 RT-qPCR 方法(Allplex Respiratory Panels 和 Allplex SARS-CoV-2 Assay)提取和测试 RNA。比较了两种方法的一致性、灵敏度、特异性和分析性能。与传统检测相比,Switching RT-qPCR 检测的临床敏感性为 93.6%,特异性为 100%,总体一致性率超过 96%。大多数病毒靶标(尤其是 RSV A、AdV 和 hMPV)的分析灵敏度相当或更高。双工检测形式能够在每个反应中同时有效检测两个目标,从而减少总体测试时间,同时保持分析准确性。这种转换 RT-qPCR 检测为呼吸道病毒检测提供了可靠、快速且高效的替代方案。其简化的双工形式以及与标准分子诊断的高度一致性表明其在常规临床实验室中的潜在实用性。

papers.title: Clinician-Reported Respiratory Viral Testing and Intended Management of Community-Acquired Respiratory Viral Infections in Haematology and Haematopoietic Cell Transplantation: An International Exploratory Survey
papers.abstract: Background: Community-acquired respiratory viruses (CARVs) cause significant morbidity and mortality in patients with haematological malignancies and those undergoing haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Despite this, clinical management remains variable. This study evaluated clinicians’ awareness, diagnostic practices, and treatment approaches to major respiratory viruses in this high-risk population. Methods: An international electronic survey using non-probability convenience sampling was conducted among haematology, oncology, intensive care and emergency medicine physicians. Four real-life clinical cases were converted into standardised vignettes covering human metapneumovirus (HMPV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human parainfluenza virus (HPIV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The questionnaire assessed reported testing strategies and intended management, including antiviral and immunoprophylactic interventions. Responses were analysed descriptively; no inferential between-group comparisons were performed. Results: Ninety-eight clinicians from 26 countries responded. Diagnostic approaches, including testing indications and panel selection, varied among respondents. For HMPV and HPIV, respondents mainly reported supportive care, immunoglobulin replacement, and infection-control measures in the absence of established pathogen-specific interventions. RSV practice was heterogeneous: systemic ribavirin was considered by 45/96 (46.9%) respondents, including 34/96 (35.4%) when guided by an immunodeficiency score. IAV management was more consistent, with reported availability of vaccination and antiviral therapy and frequent use of post-exposure prophylaxis. Conclusions: Within this international convenience sample, clinicians reported variation in respiratory viral testing and in how results informed intended management. Because sampling was non-probability-based and respondent groups were small and unevenly distributed, the findings should not be interpreted as representative estimates of international practice. IAV testing was most consistently linked to established treatment and prevention, RSV showed greater therapeutic and preventive heterogeneity, and HMPV/HPIV testing primarily informed infection control, monitoring and antimicrobial stewardship.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 社区获得性呼吸道病毒 (CARV) 在血液系统恶性肿瘤患者和接受造血细胞移植 (HCT) 的患者中引起显着的发病率和 死亡率。尽管如此,临床管理仍然存在差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在血液学、肿瘤学、重症监护和急诊医学医生中进行了一项使用非概率便利抽样的国际电子调查。四个真实的临床病例被转换成标准化的小插图,涵盖 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、人类偏肺病毒 (HMPV)、人类副流感病毒 (HPIV) 和甲型流感病毒 (IAV)。
elements_zh.methods: 调查问卷评估了报告的检测策略和预期管理,包括 抗病毒药物 和免疫预防干预措施。对答复进行描述性分析;没有进行推断组间比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 来自 26 个国家的 98 名临床医生做出了回应。诊断方法(包括测试适应症和小组选择)因受访者而异。对于 HMPV 和 HPIV,受访者主要报告了支持性护理、免疫球蛋白替代和感染控制措施,但缺乏既定的病原体特异性干预措施。RSV 实践存在差异:45/96 (46.9%) 的受访者考虑全身使用利巴韦林,其中在免疫缺陷评分指导下考虑使用利巴韦林为 34/96 (35.4%)。IAV 管理更加一致,据报告可使用 疫苗接种 和 抗病毒药物 治疗,并经常使用暴露后预防。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在这个国际便利样本中,临床医生报告了呼吸道病毒检测以及结果如何通知预期管理的差异。由于抽样不是基于概率的,而且受访者群体规模较小且分布不均,因此调查结果不应被解释为国际实践的代表性估计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了高危人群中 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 标准化诊断和管理方案的必要性。他们还建议需要进一步研究以提高临床实践的一致性并制定有针对性的干预措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究使用了非概率便利抽样,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。此外,受访者群体规模小且分布不均,降低了证据的强度,调查结果不应被解释为国际实践的代表性估计。

papers.title: Analiza hematoloških parametara u djece s bronhiolitisom uzrokovanim respiratornim sincicijskim virusom The analysis of haematological parameters in children with bronchiolitis caused by respiratory syncytial virus
papers.abstract: Cilj: Cilj je ovog presječnog istraživanja ispitati povezanost hematoloških parametara u djece s bronhiolitisom uzrokovanim respiratornim sincicijskim virusom s kliničkim karakteristikama bolesti te analizirati njihovu moguću prediktivnu vrijednost. Ispitanici i metode: Istraživanje je presječno, provedeno na uzorku od 100 djece hospitalizirane na Odjelu pedijatrije Opće županijske bolnice u Požegi od 2010. godine zbog bronhiolitisa uzrokovanog respiratornim sincicijskim virusom. Podatci o pacijentima i tijeku bolesti prikupljeni su iz medicinske dokumentacije. Svim pacijentima s kliničkom slikom bronhiolitisa kojima je iz brisa nazofarinksa izoliran respiracijski sincicijski virus, učinjena je kompletna krvna slika i C-reaktivni protein. U statističkoj obradi korišteni su test 2, Mann-Whitneyev test, Spearmanov koeficijent korelacije (Rho) te binarna logistička regresija. Rezultati: S obzirom na ovisnost o kisiku, utvrđene su statistički značajno niže vrijednosti eritrocita (p = 0,030) te značajno više ispitanika s vrijednostima trombocita iznad referentnog raspona (p = 0,030) u skupini koja je ovisna o kisiku, u odnosu na ispitanike koji nisu ovisni o kisiku. C-reaktivni protein nije povezan s prisutnošću pneumonije i ovisnosti o kisiku. Što su više vrijednosti trombocita, a niže vrijednosti MPV-a, to je i dulje trajanje bolesti. Zaključak: Djeca koja tijekom hospitalizacije zbog akutnog bronhiolitisa uzrokovanog respiratornim sincicijskim virusom imaju niže vrijednosti eritrocita i više vrijednosti trombocita iz periferne krvi, imaju veći rizik za ovisnost o kisiku tijekom liječenja, a samim time i za teži tijek bolesti. C-reaktivni protein nije statistički značajno povezan s težinom ili trajanjem bolesti.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the association between haematological parameters and clinical characteristics in children with bronchiolitis caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). It was a cross-sectional study conducted on 100 children hospitalized at the Department of Pediatrics in Požega General Hospital in 2010 due to RSV bronchiolitis. Complete blood count and C-reactive protein were performed on all patients with clinical features of bronchiolitis confirmed by RSV isolation from nasal swabs. The results showed statistically significant lower erythrocyte counts and higher platelet counts in children dependent on oxygen therapy compared to those not dependent. The authors interpreted these findings as indicating a higher risk of oxygen dependency and more severe disease progression in children with lower erythrocyte counts and higher platelet counts. The study suggests potential utility in identifying children at risk for severe RSV bronchiolitis. However, the analysis relied on data from medical records, which may limit precision and generalizability. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature and potential for confounding factors.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: Istraživanje je presječno, provedeno na uzorku od 100 djece hospitalizirane na Odjelu pedijatrije Opće županijske bolnice u Požegi od 2010. godine zbog bronhiolitisa uzrokovanog respiratornim sincicijskim virusom.
analysis_en.methods: Podatci o pacijentima i tijeku bolesti prikupljeni su iz medicinske dokumentacije. Svim pacijentima s kliničkom slikom bronhiolitisa kojima je iz brisa nazofarinksa izoliran respiracijski sincicijski virus, učinjena je kompletna krvna slika i C-reaktivni protein.
analysis_en.main_results: S obzirom na ovisnost o kisiku, utvrđene su statistički značajno niže vrijednosti eritrocita (p = 0,030) te značajno više ispitanika s vrijednostima trombocita iznad referentnog raspona (p = 0,030) u skupini koja je ovisna o kisiku, u odnosu na ispitanike koji nisu ovisni o kisiku.

papers.title: PREVENCIÓN DE LAS INFECCIONES SEVERAS POR VIRUS SINCITIAL RESPIRATORIO EN LACTANTES EN EL PERÚ: RECOMENDACIONES BASADAS EN LA METODOLOGÍA GRADE PREVENTION OF SEVERE RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS INFECTIONS IN INFANTS IN PERU: RECOMMENDATIONS BASED ON THE GRADE METHODOLOGY
papers.abstract: Introducción: El virus sincitial respiratorio (VSR) es la principal causa de infección respiratoria aguda baja en lactantes y representa una importante carga de morbilidad, hospitalización y mortalidad, especialmente durante los primeros meses de vida en países de ingresos bajos y medianos como el Perú. Objetivo: Desarrollar recomendaciones basadas en evidencia para prevenir la enfermedad grave por VSR en lactantes en el Perú. Métodos: Se elaboró una guía de práctica clínica utilizando la metodología GRADE. Se formularon cinco preguntas clínicas estructuradas en formato PICO y se realizó una revisión sistemática de la evidencia en bases de datos biomédicas. La certeza de la evidencia se evaluó considerando el riesgo de sesgo, la consistencia, la precisión y la aplicabilidad. Se utilizó un marco de la Evidencia a la Decisión (EtD) para formular recomendaciones. Resultados: Se recomienda la vacunación materna entre las 32 y 36 semanas de gestación para reducir la enfermedad grave y las hospitalizaciones por VSR en lactantes (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En lactantes no protegidos por vacunación materna, se recomienda administrar nirsevimab (recomendación fuerte a favor, evidencia alta). En prematuros y en poblaciones de alto riesgo, nirsevimab se considera la estrategia preferida, con recomendaciones fuertes o condicionales según el subgrupo y la disponibilidad de evidencia directa. Conclusión: Las estrategias de inmunoprofilaxis contra el VSR, basadas en la vacunación materna y el uso de un anticuerpo monoclonal (nirsevimab), tienen el potencial de reducir sustancialmente la carga de enfermedad en lactantes en el Perú, y su implementación programada debe considerarse una prioridad de salud pública.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop evidence-based recommendations for preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections in infants in Peru. Using the GRADE methodology, five structured PICO clinical questions were formulated, and a systematic review of biomedical databases was conducted. The results indicated that maternal vaccination between 32 and 36 weeks of gestation is strongly recommended to reduce severe RSV disease and hospitalizations in infants, with high-quality evidence. Additionally, nirsevimab is strongly recommended for infants not protected by maternal vaccination, and it is considered the preferred strategy for preterm infants and high-risk populations, with strong or conditional recommendations based on subgroup availability. The authors interpreted these findings as having significant potential to reduce the disease burden in Peruvian infants, highlighting the importance of implementing these strategies as a public health priority. The evidence strength was assessed as high, with the certainty of evidence evaluated based on bias risk, consistency, precision, and applicability. However, the study is limited by its reliance on abstract-only evidence and the absence of detailed statistical or methodological procedures.
