analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the potential of urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, addressing the gap in understanding their utility compared to sewer-based systems.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Kampala, Uganda, with ten drainage channel sampling points and 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples collected during two campaigns in March and September-October 2025.
analysis.methods: A multi-target panel was quantified using digital PCR, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among other pathogens, and samples were normalized by Pepper Mild Mottle Virus (PMMoV) as a fecal indicator.
analysis.main_results: Respiratory syncytial virus was rarely detected in both drainage channels and wastewater treatment plant influents, with concentrations varying across sampling locations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The low detection rates of RSV suggest that it may not be as prevalent in the sampled non-sewered settings compared to other pathogens, but the study highlights the potential of drainage surveillance to provide spatially resolved public health data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that drainage-based surveillance could be a valuable tool for monitoring RSV in non-sewered urban areas, offering insights into disease prevalence at the neighborhood level.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are limited by the low detection rates of RSV, and the comparability of drainage and wastewater surveillance varied by location and pathogen, indicating the need for further targeted research.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the feasibility of using urban drainage channels for multi-pathogen wastewater and environmental surveillance in non-sewered settings, focusing on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Kampala, Uganda. It collected 255 drainage channel and 54 wastewater treatment plant influent samples during two campaigns in 2025. RSV was rarely detected in both sample types, with concentrations varying across locations. The low detection rates suggest limited prevalence in the sampled areas, but the study highlights the potential of drainage surveillance to provide spatially resolved public health data. The findings imply that drainage-based monitoring could be useful for tracking RSV in non-sewered urban environments, though further research is needed to confirm these results. The study's limitations include the variability in comparability between drainage and wastewater samples, which may affect the reliability of surveillance data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在探索城市排水沟在非污水收集环境中用于多病原体废水和环境监测的潜力,以填补其在效用方面相较于污水收集系统的认知缺口。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 研究在乌干达坎帕拉市进行,共设置10个排水沟采样点,并在2025年3月及9-10月两个时段收集了54份废水治疗厂进水样本。
elements_zh.methods: 采用数字PCR技术对多靶标面板进行定量分析,其中包括呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等病原体,并以辣椒轻斑驳病毒(PMMoV)作为粪便指示剂对样本进行标准化处理。
elements_zh.main_results: 呼吸道合胞病毒 在排水沟和废水 治疗 工厂进水中很少检测到,不同采样地点的浓度各不相同。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RSV 的低检出率表明,与其他病原体相比,它在采样的非下水道环境中可能并不那么普遍,但该研究强调了排水 监测 提供空间解析公共卫生数据的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于排水系统的 监测 可能是监测无下水道城市地区 RSV 的宝贵工具,可提供对社区层面疾病 患病率 的深入了解。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的结果受到RSV检出率低的限制,并且排水和废水监测的可比性因地点和病原体而异,表明需要进一步开展有针对性的研究。

papers.title: Anellovirus-mediated interferon dysregulation enhances virus-induced lung injury.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the lung virome after lung transplantation and test whether anelloviruses modulate innate immune responses that influence susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury. RATIONALE: The lung virome (LV) and its interactions with the host immune system leading to allograft injury after lung -transplantation are not well characterized. METHODS: Shotgun metagenomics and qPCR was performed on a multicenter BAL/serum cohort from lung transplant recipients (LTRs). Viral constructs from a Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in primary bronchial epithelial cells (PBECs) or airways of C57BL/6 mice with and without exposure to influenza A virus (IAV) or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LV in LTRs was dominated by viruses from the family Anelloviridae. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) LV was characterized by the enrichment of BTV. Validation in an independent cohort confirmed BTV abundance in CLAD BAL fluid, serum, and lung tissues. BTV ORF1 protein (kV1) suppressed PBEC IFN-α and IFN-γ responses by preventing intranuclear STAT translocation. Co-culture of IAV or RSV in kV1-transfected PBECs significantly augmented replication of RSV and IAV and increased cellular injury. Likewise, in vivo transfection of kV1 increased replication and lung injury associated with IAV. CONCLUSIONS: Our work illuminates a novel virus-associated dysregulation of host interferon responses that promote lung injury associated with respiratory viral infections and, in part, explain differential host responses to viral infections after lung transplantation.
papers.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of anelloviruses in modulating innate immune responses and their impact on susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury after lung transplantation. Using shotgun metagenomics and qPCR, the research characterizes the lung virome in transplant recipients and identifies anelloviruses as dominant. Further, viral constructs from Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in bronchial epithelial cells and mice models, revealing that BTV suppresses interferon responses. Co-culture experiments showed that BTV enhances replication and cellular injury of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza A virus (IAV). The study concludes that anellovirus-mediated interferon dysregulation may contribute to lung injury associated with viral infections, potentially explaining differential host responses post-transplant. While the findings are significant for understanding viral interactions with the immune system, the study is limited to abstract-only data and relies on in vitro and in vivo models, which may not fully translate to human conditions. These results could inform future research on targeted therapeutic strategies for lung transplant recipients.

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: To characterize the lung virome after lung transplantation and test whether anelloviruses modulate innate immune responses that influence susceptibility to respiratory viral-associated allograft injury. RATIONALE: The lung virome (LV) and its interactions with the host immune system leading to allograft injury after lung -transplantation are not well characterized. METHODS: Shotgun metagenomics and qPCR was performed on a multicenter BAL/serum cohort from lung transplant recipients (LTRs). Viral constructs from a Betatorquevirus clade (BTV) and group 2 torque teno viruses were transfected in primary bronchial epithelial cells (PBECs) or airways of C57BL/6 mice with and without exposure to influenza A virus (IAV) or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LV in LTRs was dominated by viruses from the family Anelloviridae. Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) LV was characterized by the enrichment of BTV. Validation in an independent cohort confirmed BTV abundance in CLAD BAL fluid, serum, and lung tissues. BTV ORF1 protein (kV1) suppressed PBEC IFN-α and IFN-γ responses by preventing intranuclear STAT translocation. Co-culture of IAV or RSV in kV1-transfected PBECs significantly augmented replication of RSV and IAV and increased cellular injury. Likewise, in vivo transfection of kV1 increased replication and lung injury associated with IAV. CONCLUSIONS: Our work illuminates a novel virus-associated dysregulation of host interferon responses that promote lung injury associated with respiratory viral infections and, in part, explain differential host responses to viral infections after lung transplantation.

papers.title: Understanding RSV Resurgence Following COVID-19 in Ontario, Canada: Evaluating the Roles of Contact Patterns and Maternal Immunity
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of hospitalization in infancy, with severe outcomes influenced by both contact patterns and passive immunity. Non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) during the COVID-19 pandemic suppressed RSV circulation and reduced opportunities for maternal immune boosting, potentially altering protection among newborns. We evaluated whether incorporating time-varying maternal immunity improves the ability of an age-structured transmission model to predict post-pandemic RSV hospitalization patterns in infants. Methods: We analyzed population-based RSV hospitalizations among Ontario (Canada) infants (<1 year) from July 2, 2017 to June 25, 2024, using linked administrative databases. A deterministic compartmental model across seven age classes was calibrated against pre-pandemic data using Latin Hypercube Sampling. We compared a model incorporating time-varying contact rates alone against a specification that additionally included time-varying maternal immunity. Results: Both specifications accurately reproduced pre-pandemic seasonality and macro-level post-pandemic resurgence features. The constant maternal immunity model showed slightly better accuracy in capturing the 2021/22 peak compared to the time-varying maternal immunity specification. However, both qualitatively captured the continued near-absence of RSV and the observed peak was captured within the 95% credible intervals. While both models precisely captured the timing and overwhelming surge of admissions that occurred in 2022/23, they failed to capture the premature peak timing and magnitude in 2023/24. Conclusions: Incorporating time-varying maternal immunity did not improve model accuracy post-pandemic. While maternal protection is essential for evaluating infant immunizations, population-level contact shifts primarily shaped post-pandemic RSV seasonality, indicating that models must account for these mechanisms of RSV transmission dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the resurgence of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Ontario, Canada, following the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on the roles of contact patterns and maternal immunity. The research question centers on whether incorporating time-varying maternal immunity into an age-structured transmission model improves predictions of post-pandemic RSV hospitalization patterns in infants. The study design involves analyzing population-based RSV hospitalization data from 2017 to 2024 and comparing two models: one with time-varying contact rates and another with time-varying maternal immunity. The methods include deterministic compartmental modeling across seven age classes, calibrated using Latin Hypercube Sampling. The main results show that both models accurately reproduced pre-pandemic seasonality and macro-level post-pandemic resurgence features, with the constant maternal immunity model slightly better at capturing the 2021/22 peak. However, both models failed to capture the premature peak timing and magnitude in 2023/24. The authors interpret these findings to indicate that population-level contact shifts, rather than maternal immunity, primarily shaped post-pandemic RSV seasonality. This has implications for public health modeling and suggests that future studies should account for contact dynamics in predicting RSV outbreaks. The evidence is moderate in strength due to its reliance on abstract-only data and model outputs.

papers.title: Editorial: Viral co-infections: challenges and therapeutic approaches
papers.abstract: While influenza virus co-infections may be infrequent, combined bacterial or mycoplasma infections are much more commonplace and may give rise to increased symptomology and clinical outcomes. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1719387/full carried out a retrospective cohort study utilising data from the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL)-positive, methicillin-susceptible ST22 strains were found to cause fatal outcomes in patients co-infected with influenza A or SARS-CoV-2, associated with severe leukopenia. Similarly, co-infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is frequently documented. To examine this important but understudied coinfection, Ma et al. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1787294/full? established a model in hamsters with H1NI (swine flu) which demonstrated that H1N1 infected animals which received a follow up Mp challenge exhibited significantly more severe histopathological lesions, higher pathogen loads, and dysregulated cytokine responses compared to other infection groups. A comprehensive review by Lei and colleagues discussed primary mechanisms of Influenza-mediated susceptibility to bacterial infection, with particular focus on epithelial barrier damage, immune cell dysfunction and the roles of specific immune cells, and their effector pathways in inducing hyperinflammatory responses aa well as treatment options. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1673643/full . The authors emphasise that an in depth understanding of the interactions between the pathogens and the host will assist in the development of therapeutics for the prevention and treatment of post-influenza bacterial infection.Co-infections are a well, established fundamental area of research for Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) over many years. The importance of both genomic and immunological approaches to understanding HIV strain recombination, co-infections and vaccine efficacy in HIV infected individuals, are emphasised in 2 articles in this issue. A study by Ling and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript shows that circulating recombinant forms (CRFs) play a critical role in the global transmission of HIV-1 with further second-generation recombinant viruses, derived from the original CRFs, continually emerging. Furthermore, these CRFs are associated with critical changes in co-receptor tropism. This study strongly supports the importance of sustained genomic surveillance for prevention strategies. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined whether there was cross-protection from the humoral immune response of immunocompromised populations of people living with HIV to both infection with existing covid sub-lineages and subsequent covid vaccines. The study highlighted the crucial need for regular monitoring of immune responses to new covid vaccines targeting emerging variants in this category of individuals. Another immunologically challenged group are patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) receiving maintenance haemodialysis who are predisposed to anaemia. A study by Özsoy and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript raised and examined concerns that prior B19V Parvovirus infection may contribute to anaemia severity or resistance to erythropoiesisstimulating agents (ESAs).In addition to study of co-infections in human populations, research on co-infection in animal species is an important area for veterinary medicine, understanding and utilising natural virus models and for surveillance and protection against zoonotic diseases. Bats are natural reservoirs for many viruses but with information on hepatitis viruses limited. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined the diversity and evolution of bat hepatitis B viruses (BtHBVs) and their co-infection with bat hepatitis D virus (BtHDV) in bats in China and showed that they are natural hosts for both viruses.Advances in genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models reveal how pathogen interactions, immune responses, and infection timing shape disease progression. In addition, there remains an urgent need for specific antiviral therapeutics, as exemplified by 3 papers in this issue. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is of interest to identify and target new substances not currently used for conventional pharmaceutical treatments. A systematic review by Zeng and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined herbal agents documented in classical TCM texts for the treatment of Tianxing fever (closely related to dengue virus) with the aim of guiding clinical practice and modern drug development for dengue prevention and treatment. papers.title_original: Editorial: Viral co-infections: challenges and therapeutic approaches

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens, other viruses, and immune responses. It examines the clinical implications, mechanisms, and therapeutic approaches for managing RSV co-infections, with an emphasis on RSV-A and RSV-B subtypes. The central question is how co-infections affect disease severity and immune responses in RSV-infected individuals.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a combination of studies, including a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. It also references a study on hamsters with H1N1 infection and a subsequent challenge with Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which demonstrated severe histopathological lesions and dysregulated cytokine responses. The review includes a systematic analysis of herbal agents in traditional Chinese medicine for treating Tianxing fever, which is closely related to dengue virus, and a review of monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals for RSV.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that co-infections with RSV and bacterial pathogens can significantly worsen clinical outcomes. It also underscores the importance of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding pathogen interactions and immune responses. The findings suggest that RSV co-infections are a critical area for research, particularly in high-risk populations and for developing targeted therapies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while co-infections are well-documented in some contexts, there is limited evidence on the specific mechanisms of RSV co-infections with other viruses. Additionally, the role of traditional Chinese medicine in RSV treatment remains understudied, and there is a need for more research on the interactions between RSV and other pathogens in different host populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for further research into the mechanisms of RSV co-infections, especially with bacterial and other viral pathogens. It also emphasizes the need for improved surveillance, development of specific antiviral therapeutics, and exploration of alternative treatments such as traditional Chinese medicine. These efforts are crucial for managing RSV-related diseases and improving outcomes in vulnerable populations.

analysis.summary_en: This editorial explores the challenges and therapeutic approaches for managing co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens and other viruses. It highlights the clinical significance of RSV co-infections, especially in high-risk populations, and discusses the role of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding these interactions. The review also emphasizes the need for targeted therapies and the potential of traditional Chinese medicine in treating RSV-related conditions. Despite some progress, there remain unresolved questions about the specific mechanisms of RSV co-infections and the effectiveness of current interventions, underscoring the importance of continued research and surveillance.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on co-infections involving respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), particularly in the context of interactions with bacterial pathogens, other viruses, and immune responses. It examines the clinical implications, mechanisms, and therapeutic approaches for managing RSV co-infections, with an emphasis on RSV-A and RSV-B subtypes. The central question is how co-infections affect disease severity and immune responses in RSV-infected individuals.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a combination of studies, including a retrospective cohort study conducted at the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. It also references a study on hamsters with H1N1 infection and a subsequent challenge with Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which demonstrated severe histopathological lesions and dysregulated cytokine responses. The review includes a systematic analysis of herbal agents in traditional Chinese medicine for treating Tianxing fever, which is closely related to dengue virus, and a review of monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals for RSV.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review highlights that co-infections with RSV and bacterial pathogens can significantly worsen clinical outcomes. It also underscores the importance of genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models in understanding pathogen interactions and immune responses. The findings suggest that RSV co-infections are a critical area for research, particularly in high-risk populations and for developing targeted therapies.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while co-infections are well-documented in some contexts, there is limited evidence on the specific mechanisms of RSV co-infections with other viruses. Additionally, the role of traditional Chinese medicine in RSV treatment remains understudied, and there is a need for more research on the interactions between RSV and other pathogens in different host populations.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review calls for further research into the mechanisms of RSV co-infections, especially with bacterial and other viral pathogens. It also emphasizes the need for improved surveillance, development of specific antiviral therapeutics, and exploration of alternative treatments such as traditional Chinese medicine. These efforts are crucial for managing RSV-related diseases and improving outcomes in vulnerable populations.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是涉及 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的合并感染,特别是在与细菌病原体、其他病毒和 免疫应答 相互作用的情况下。它研究了管理 RSV 合并感染的临床意义、机制和治疗方法,重点是 RSV-A 和 RSV-B 亚型。核心问题是合并感染如何影响 RSV 感染者的疾病严重程度和 免疫应答。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于多项研究的结合,包括在苏州大学第四附属医院进行的回顾性 队列研究 研究。它还引用了一项针对感染 H1N1 的仓鼠以及随后受到肺炎支原体攻击的研究,该研究显示出严重的组织病理学病变和细胞因子反应失调。该综述包括对治疗与登革热病毒密切相关的天星热的中药中草药的系统分析,以及针对 RSV 的单克隆抗体和小分子 抗病毒药物 的综述。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述强调,RSV 和细菌病原体的共同感染会显着恶化临床结果。它还强调了 基因组监测、免疫学研究和实验模型在理解病原体相互作用和 免疫应答 方面的重要性。研究结果表明,RSV 合并感染是研究的一个关键领域,特别是在高危人群中,以及开发靶向治疗。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,虽然在某些情况下混合感染有详细记录,但有关 RSV 与其他病毒混合感染的具体机制的证据有限。此外,中药在RSV 治疗中的作用仍有待研究,并且需要对不同宿主人群中RSV与其他病原体之间的相互作用进行更多研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述呼吁进一步研究 RSV 联合感染的机制,特别是细菌和其他病毒病原体的联合感染。它还强调需要改进监测、开发特定的抗病毒药物疗法以及探索替代治疗(例如中药)。这些努力对于管理 RSV 相关疾病和改善弱势群体的治疗效果至关重要。

papers.source_body_en: While influenza virus co-infections may be infrequent, combined bacterial or mycoplasma infections are much more commonplace and may give rise to increased symptomology and clinical outcomes. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1719387/full carried out a retrospective cohort study utilising data from the Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Soochow University. Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL)-positive, methicillin-susceptible ST22 strains were found to cause fatal outcomes in patients co-infected with influenza A or SARS-CoV-2, associated with severe leukopenia. Similarly, co-infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is frequently documented. To examine this important but understudied coinfection, Ma et al. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2026.1787294/full? established a model in hamsters with H1NI (swine flu) which demonstrated that H1N1 infected animals which received a follow up Mp challenge exhibited significantly more severe histopathological lesions, higher pathogen loads, and dysregulated cytokine responses compared to other infection groups. A comprehensive review by Lei and colleagues discussed primary mechanisms of Influenza-mediated susceptibility to bacterial infection, with particular focus on epithelial barrier damage, immune cell dysfunction and the roles of specific immune cells, and their effector pathways in inducing hyperinflammatory responses aa well as treatment options. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2025.1673643/full . The authors emphasise that an in depth understanding of the interactions between the pathogens and the host will assist in the development of therapeutics for the prevention and treatment of post-influenza bacterial infection.Co-infections are a well, established fundamental area of research for Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) over many years. The importance of both genomic and immunological approaches to understanding HIV strain recombination, co-infections and vaccine efficacy in HIV infected individuals, are emphasised in 2 articles in this issue. A study by Ling and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript shows that circulating recombinant forms (CRFs) play a critical role in the global transmission of HIV-1 with further second-generation recombinant viruses, derived from the original CRFs, continually emerging. Furthermore, these CRFs are associated with critical changes in co-receptor tropism. This study strongly supports the importance of sustained genomic surveillance for prevention strategies. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined whether there was cross-protection from the humoral immune response of immunocompromised populations of people living with HIV to both infection with existing covid sub-lineages and subsequent covid vaccines. The study highlighted the crucial need for regular monitoring of immune responses to new covid vaccines targeting emerging variants in this category of individuals. Another immunologically challenged group are patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) receiving maintenance haemodialysis who are predisposed to anaemia. A study by Özsoy and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript raised and examined concerns that prior B19V Parvovirus infection may contribute to anaemia severity or resistance to erythropoiesisstimulating agents (ESAs).In addition to study of co-infections in human populations, research on co-infection in animal species is an important area for veterinary medicine, understanding and utilising natural virus models and for surveillance and protection against zoonotic diseases. Bats are natural reservoirs for many viruses but with information on hepatitis viruses limited. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined the diversity and evolution of bat hepatitis B viruses (BtHBVs) and their co-infection with bat hepatitis D virus (BtHDV) in bats in China and showed that they are natural hosts for both viruses.Advances in genomic surveillance, immunological studies, and experimental models reveal how pathogen interactions, immune responses, and infection timing shape disease progression. In addition, there remains an urgent need for specific antiviral therapeutics, as exemplified by 3 papers in this issue. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is of interest to identify and target new substances not currently used for conventional pharmaceutical treatments. A systematic review by Zeng and colleagues https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined herbal agents documented in classical TCM texts for the treatment of Tianxing fever (closely related to dengue virus) with the aim of guiding clinical practice and modern drug development for dengue prevention and treatment. A further review by Liu et al. https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript comprehensively summarises the current status of Respiratory Syncytial Virus monoclonal antibodies and small-molecule antivirals. A third experimental study by Liang and team https://research-topic-management-app.frontiersin.org/manage/66895/manuscript examined an alternative therapeutic approach to vaccines for porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Mogroside V, a triterpenoid compound (derived from Siraitia grosvenorii) which has previously been shown to exhibit diverse biological activities including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer properties, with the capacity to scavenge free radicals and mitigate oxidative stress was assessed in vitro. This compound not only directly inhibited PRRSV replication but also significantly upregulated the gene expression of immunomodulatory cytokines.• Co-infections are generally uncommon but can significantly worsen disease severity, particularly in viral-bacterial combinations or high-risk populations.• Pathogen interactions and infection order play a critical role in clinical outcomes and immune responses.• Ongoing surveillance, vaccination strategies, and development of targeted therapies are essential to address the evolving complexity of co-infections.Overall, the research underscores the need for continued monitoring, integrated prevention strategies, and improved therapeutic approaches to manage complex co-infections.

是一种三萜化合物(源自罗汉果),此前已被证明具有多种生物活性,包括抗氧化、抗炎和抗癌特性,并具有清除自由基和减轻氧化应激的能力,并在体外进行了评估。该化合物不仅直接抑制 PRRSV 复制,而且显着上调免疫调节细胞因子的基因表达。• 合并感染通常不常见,但会显着恶化疾病严重程度,特别是在病毒-细菌组合或高危人群中。• 病原体相互作用和感染顺序在临床结果和 免疫应答 中发挥着关键作用。• 持续的 analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于多项研究的结合,包括在苏州大学第四附属医院进行的回顾性 队列研究 研究。它还引用了一项针对感染 H1N1 的仓鼠以及随后受到肺炎支原体攻击的研究,该研究显示出严重的组织病理学病变和细胞因子反应失调。该综述包括对治疗与登革热病毒密切相关的天星热的中药中草药的系统分析,以及针对 RSV 的单克隆抗体和小分子 抗病毒药物 的综述。

papers.title: Anticipating the Next Week: Calibrated Prediction of State-Level Respiratory Illness Escalation from Public Surveillance Data
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory-virus surveillance teams need early, credible, and low-burden signals of worsening activity. Current dashboards describe recent activity well, but they are less directly designed to rank jurisdictions that are already at moderate influenza-like illness (ILI) activity and may cross into high activity in the next reporting week. Methods We conducted a retrospective state-week prediction study using public U.S. outpatient ILI surveillance from CDC ILINet, accessed through Delphi Epidata FluView, and regional RSV and SARS-CoV-2 nucleic-acid test positivity from CDC NREVSS. The target was transition from moderate state-specific ILI activity at week t to high activity at week t + 1. State-specific thresholds, preprocessing, hyperparameter tuning, probability calibration, and alert-threshold selection were estimated from development data only. Candidate models were selected by rolling-origin cross-validation and evaluated once on a later chronological holdout. Held-out uncertainty was quantified with state-cluster bootstrap confidence intervals. Results The modelling cohort contained 4,232 moderate state-weeks from 51 jurisdictions. The holdout period contained 943 state-weeks and 127 moderate-to-high transitions. The selected calibrated logistic regression model achieved AUROC 0.877, average precision 0.529, F1 0.594, precision 0.589, recall 0.598, and specificity 0.935. It issued 129 alerts and identified 76 of 127 transitions, whereas an alert-all-moderate baseline identified all transitions but required 943 alerts. The most useful signals were proximity to the state-specific high-activity threshold, seasonal timing, recent ILI history, reporting volume, and lagged RSV/SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Conclusions A simple calibrated surveillance model reduced alert burden while retaining most short-horizon escalations. The study should be interpreted as a transparent benchmark for respiratory-surveillance triage research, not as a deployed public health decision rule. Its contribution is an evaluation framework that combines temporal cross-validation, independent temporal testing, bootstrap uncertainty, calibration, threshold analysis, and explicit reporting that true external validation remains unavailable.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a low-burden surveillance model to predict respiratory illness escalation at the state level. Using public U.S. data from CDC ILINet and NREVSS, the model focused on transitions from moderate to high influenza-like illness (ILI) activity. The calibrated logistic regression model achieved moderate performance metrics, including an AUROC of 0.877 and F1 score of 0.594, while significantly reducing the number of alerts needed compared to a baseline approach. The model's most useful signals included proximity to high-activity thresholds, seasonal timing, and lagged RSV/SARS-CoV-2 positivity. The study emphasizes the importance of calibrated models in improving surveillance efficiency but notes that true external validation remains unavailable. These findings offer a framework for future research in respiratory virus surveillance and triage systems.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒 监测 团队需要早期、可靠且低负担的活动恶化信号。目前的仪表板很好地描述了近期的活动,但它们的设计不太直接地对已经处于中度流感样疾病 (ILI) 活动的辖区进行排名,并且可能在下一个报告周进入高活动度。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们利用来自 CDC ILINEt 的美国公立门诊 ILI 监测(通过 Delphi Epidata FluView 访问)以及来自 CDC NREVSS 的区域 RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 核酸检测阳性结果,进行了一项回顾性州周预测研究。目标是从 t 周的中度州特定 ILI 活动过渡到 t + 1 周的高活动。
elements_zh.methods: 仅根据开发数据估计特定于状态的阈值、预处理、超参数调整、概率校准和警报阈值选择。通过滚动源交叉验证来选择候选模型,并在稍后按时间顺序保留时进行一次评估。保留的不确定性通过状态簇引导置信区间进行量化。
elements_zh.main_results: 建模 队列研究 包含来自 51 个司法管辖区的 4,232 个中等州周。坚持期包含 943 个状态周和 127 个中度到高度的转换。所选校准逻辑回归模型的 AUROC 0.877、平均精度 0.529、F1 0.594、精度 0.589、召回率 0.598 和特异性 0.935。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 简单的校准 监测 模型减轻了警报负担,同时保留了大多数短期升级。最有用的信号是接近州特定的高活动阈值、季节性时间、近期流感样病例历史、报告量以及滞后的 RSV/SARS-CoV-2 阳性率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究为呼吸道 监测 分类研究提供了透明的基准,可以为开发更有效的呼吸道病毒 监测 系统提供信息。它强调了校准模型在减轻警报负担、同时保持预测活动升级的准确性方面的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究应被解释为呼吸系统 监测 分类研究的透明基准,而不是部署的公共卫生决策规则。它的贡献是一个评估框架,结合了时间交叉验证、独立时间测试、引导不确定性、校准、阈值分析和明确报告真正的外部验证仍然不可用。

papers.title: Effectiveness of RSV Prevention Strategies in US Infants: 2024-2025.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: In 2023, 2 products, a long-acting monoclonal antibody (nirsevimab) and maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination, were recommended in the United States to prevent severe RSV disease among infants in their first RSV season. Low uptake during the 2023 to 2024 RSV season limited effectiveness estimates. We estimated nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated emergency department (ED) encounters and hospitalization among US infants during the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, when uptake was higher. METHODS: We used electronic health record data from 5 health care systems in test-negative analyses of ED encounters and hospitalizations with RSV-like illness during October 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025, among infants in their first RSV season. Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness were estimated by comparing RSV-positive with RSV-negative encounters with respect to immunization status in separate logistic regression models adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, sex, calendar day, and geographic region. RESULTS: Among 3531 ED encounters and 470 hospitalizations included in the nirsevimab analyses, nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization was 62% (95% CI: 54-68) and 77% (95% CI: 61-87), respectively. Among 810 ED encounters and 187 hospitalizations included in the maternal RSV vaccine analyses, vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization was 49% (95% CI: 26-65) and 82% (95% CI: 54-93), respectively. CONCLUSION: Nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination were effective against RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalization among infants in their first RSV season. As uptake increases and additional products are recommended, monitoring infant RSV immunization effectiveness remains important.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of RSV prevention strategies, specifically nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination, in reducing RSV-associated emergency department encounters and hospitalizations among US infants during their first RSV season. The background highlights that these two products were recommended in 2023 but had limited uptake during the 2023 to 2024 season, which affected the ability to estimate their effectiveness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using electronic health record data from 5 healthcare systems during the 2024 to 2025 RSV season, focusing on infants in their first RSV season. The population included 3531 emergency department encounters and 470 hospitalizations for RSV-like illness, with separate analyses for nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness.
analysis.methods: Effectiveness was estimated through test-negative analyses of ED encounters and hospitalizations with RSV-like illness, comparing RSV-positive with RSV-negative cases based on immunization status. Logistic regression models were used, adjusting for age, race and ethnicity, sex, calendar day, and geographic region.
analysis.main_results: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated ED encounters was 62% (95% CI: 54-68), and against hospitalization was 77% (95% CI: 61-87). Maternal RSV vaccine effectiveness against ED encounters was 49% (95% CI: 26-65), and against hospitalization was 82% (95% CI: 54-93).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these results as evidence of the effectiveness of both nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination in preventing RSV-associated ED encounters and hospitalizations among infants in their first RSV season, with nirsevimab showing higher effectiveness against ED encounters compared to the maternal vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the importance of monitoring infant RSV immunization effectiveness as uptake increases and additional products are recommended, providing critical data for public health strategies and clinical decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on electronic health record data, which may have biases or missing information. However, the evidence is strong given the use of test-negative analyses and adjustment for key demographic and temporal factors, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of nirsevimab and maternal RSV vaccination in preventing RSV-associated emergency department encounters and hospitalizations among US infants during their first RSV season. Using electronic health record data from 5 healthcare systems between October 1, 2024, and March 31, 2025, the researchers conducted test-negative analyses and logistic regression models adjusted for age, race and ethnicity, sex, calendar day, and geographic region. They found nirsevimab to be 62% effective against ED encounters and 77% effective against hospitalization, while maternal RSV vaccine showed 49% and 82% effectiveness, respectively. The authors concluded that both interventions are effective, emphasizing the need for ongoing monitoring as uptake increases. The study's reliance on electronic health records introduces potential biases, but the methods and results provide a moderate level of confidence in the effectiveness of these RSV prevention strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)预防策略的有效性,具体包括尼塞韦单抗(尼塞韦单抗)和孕妇呼吸道合胞病毒疫苗(maternal RSV 疫苗),以减少美国婴儿在首个RSV流行季期间因RSV相关急诊就诊和住院的发生率。背景部分强调,这两种产品于2023年被推荐使用,但在2023至2024流行季期间的采用率有限,影响了对其有效性的评估能力。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 2024 年至 2025 年 RSV 季节期间来自 5 个医疗保健系统的电子健康记录数据进行,重点关注第一个 RSV 季节的婴儿。该人群包括 3531 例急诊科就诊病例和 470 例因 RSV 类疾病住院的病例,并对 尼塞韦单抗 和孕产妇 RSV 疫苗 有效性进行了单独分析。
elements_zh.methods: 通过对急诊科就诊和因 RSV 样疾病住院治疗的测试阴性分析,根据免疫状态比较 RSV 阳性和 RSV 阴性病例来评估有效性。使用逻辑回归模型,调整年龄、种族和民族、性别、日历日和地理区域。
elements_zh.main_results: 尼塞韦单抗 对 RSV 相关 ED 患者的有效率为 62% (95% CI: 54-68),对住院治疗的有效率为 77% (95% CI: 61-87)。母亲 RSV 疫苗 对抗 ED 的有效性为 49% (95% CI: 26-65),对抗住院治疗的有效性为 82% (95% CI: 54-93)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些结果解释为尼塞韦单抗和母体RSV 疫苗接种在预防第一个RSV季节婴儿中与RSV相关的ED遭遇和住院治疗方面的有效性的证据,与母体疫苗相比,尼塞韦单抗在预防ED遭遇方面表现出更高的有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,随着吸收率的增加和推荐其他产品,监测婴儿 RSV 免疫效果的重要性,为公共卫生策略和临床决策提供关键数据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于对电子健康记录数据的依赖,可能存在偏倚或缺失信息。然而,由于采用了检测阴性分析并针对关键人口统计学和时间因素进行了调整,证据强度较高,支持中等置信度评估。

papers.title: PIWIL4 regulates gene expression and piRNA levels in RSV-infected airway epithelial cells
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infections with significant morbidity and mortality in young children, the elderly and immunocompromised hosts. Despite its clinical burden, no effective RSV vaccine or therapy exists for infants, only prophylactic treatment. Small non-coding RNAs have emerged as important regulators of host-pathogen interactions. PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a distinct class of small non-coding RNAs known for maintaining the genome complexity and integrity in gonadal cells. However, there is growing evidence of their role in controlling gene expression in somatic cells. The biogenesis and function of piRNAs is associated with P-element Induced Wimpy testis (Piwi) proteins, whose function in the respiratory epithelium in response to infections remains largely unexplored. Here, we characterize the expression and function of the Piwi-like protein PIWIL4 in the context of RSV infection. We found that PIWIL4 is expressed in both primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells and is significantly induced at the mRNA and protein levels following RSV infection or poly I:C stimulation, a proxy of viral infection. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that PIWIL4 was primarily nuclear in uninfected cells but translocated to the cytoplasm upon RSV exposure. While siRNA-mediated knockdown of PIWIL4 did not significantly affect RSV replication, it led to decreased secretion of several cytokines, chemokines and growth factors, indicating a role in modulating host innate immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis of PIWIL4-silenced iSAE cells showed significant changes in gene expression both in basal conditions and upon RSV infection. Ingenuity Pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes underscored the role of PIWIL4 in modulation of interferon signaling, cytokine production, stress and metabolic responses, as well as airway remodeling pathways. Silencing of PIWIL4 also resulted in global alteration of piRNA expression both in uninfected and infected cells. However, the predicted targets of the differentially expressed piRNAs had limited overlap with the differentially expressed genes identified by transcriptomics, suggesting a function of PIWIL4 in regulating airway epithelial cell responses at least in part independent of piRNAs. Taken together, our study uncovers an important role for PIWIL4 in somatic cells and position it as a key regulator of airway epithelial innate immunity. A better understanding of the mechanisms by which PIWIL4 affects host cells responses following a pathogen exposure may identify novel therapeutic strategies for RSV, as well as other viral respiratory infections.

Despite its clinical burden, no effective RSV vaccine or therapy exists for infants, only prophylactic treatment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study characterized the expression and function of the Piwi-like protein PIWIL4 in the context of RSV infection. It focused on primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells, examining both baseline and infected conditions.
analysis.methods: The study used siRNA-mediated knockdown of PIWIL4 to assess its impact on RSV replication and host immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to evaluate gene expression changes in PIWIL4-silenced cells, and immunofluorescence microscopy was used to observe PIWIL4 localization.
analysis.main_results: PIWIL4 is expressed in both primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells and is significantly induced at the mRNA and protein levels following RSV infection or poly I:C stimulation. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that PIWIL4 was primarily nuclear in uninfected cells but translocated to the cytoplasm upon RSV exposure. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the role of PIWIL4 in modulating host innate immune responses and airway epithelial cell responses, at least in part independent of piRNAs. It positions PIWIL4 as a key regulator of airway epithelial innate immunity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Understanding the mechanisms by which PIWIL4 affects host cell responses following pathogen exposure may lead to the identification of novel therapeutic strategies for RSV and other viral respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on in vitro experiments using siRNA-mediated knockdown, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions. The evidence is moderate as it is derived from a single study with limited direct clinical outcomes.

The research highlights PIWIL4's involvement in innate immunity and gene expression regulation, suggesting potential therapeutic targets for RSV. While the findings are significant, the study's in vitro nature and lack of direct clinical outcomes limit the strength of the evidence, which is assessed as moderate.

papers.title_zh: PIWIL4 调节 RSV 感染的气道上皮细胞的基因表达和 piRNA 水平
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infections with significant morbidity and mortality in young children, the elderly and immunocompromised hosts. Despite its clinical burden, no effective RSV vaccine or therapy exists for infants, only prophylactic treatment. Small non-coding RNAs have emerged as important regulators of host-pathogen interactions. PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs) are a distinct class of small non-coding RNAs known for maintaining the genome complexity and integrity in gonadal cells. However, there is growing evidence of their role in controlling gene expression in somatic cells. The biogenesis and function of piRNAs is associated with P-element Induced Wimpy testis (Piwi) proteins, whose function in the respiratory epithelium in response to infections remains largely unexplored. Here, we characterize the expression and function of the Piwi-like protein PIWIL4 in the context of RSV infection. We found that PIWIL4 is expressed in both primary and immortalized small airway epithelial cells and is significantly induced at the mRNA and protein levels following RSV infection or poly I:C stimulation, a proxy of viral infection. Immunofluorescence microscopy revealed that PIWIL4 was primarily nuclear in uninfected cells but translocated to the cytoplasm upon RSV exposure. While siRNA-mediated knockdown of PIWIL4 did not significantly affect RSV replication, it led to decreased secretion of several cytokines, chemokines and growth factors, indicating a role in modulating host innate immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis of PIWIL4-silenced iSAE cells showed significant changes in gene expression both in basal conditions and upon RSV infection. Ingenuity Pathway analysis of differentially expressed genes underscored the role of PIWIL4 in modulation of interferon signaling, cytokine production, stress and metabolic responses, as well as airway remodeling pathways. Silencing of PIWIL4 also resulted in global alteration of piRNA expression both in uninfected and infected cells. However, the predicted targets of the differentially expressed piRNAs had limited overlap with the differentially expressed genes identified by transcriptomics, suggesting a function of PIWIL4 in regulating airway epithelial cell responses at least in part independent of piRNAs. Taken together, our study uncovers an important role for PIWIL4 in somatic cells and position it as a key regulator of airway epithelial innate immunity. A better understanding of the mechanisms by which PIWIL4 affects host cells responses following a pathogen exposure may identify novel therapeutic strategies for RSV, as well as other viral respiratory infections.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是急性下呼吸道感染的主要原因,在幼儿、老年人和免疫功能低下的 宿主 中具有显着的发病率和 死亡率。尽管有临床负担,但对于婴儿尚无有效的 RSV 疫苗 或疗法,只有预防性 治疗。小非编码 RNA 已成为 宿主 与病原体相互作用的重要调节因子。PIWI 相互作用 RNA (piRNA) 是一类独特的小非编码 RNA,以维持性腺细胞中 基因组 的复杂性和完整性而闻名。然而,越来越多的证据表明它们在控制体细胞基因表达方面的作用。piRNA 的生物发生和功能与 P 元素诱导的 Wimpy 睾丸 (Piwi) 蛋白相关,其在呼吸道上皮细胞中响应感染的功能在很大程度上尚未被探索。在这里,我们描述了 Piwi 样蛋白 PIWIL4 在 RSV 感染背景下的表达和功能。我们发现 PIWIL4 在原代和永生化小气道上皮细胞中表达,并且在 RSV 感染或 Poly I:C 刺激(病毒感染的代表)后在 mRNA 和蛋白质水平上显着诱导。免疫荧光显微镜显示,PIWIL4 在未感染的细胞中主要位于细胞核,但在接触 RSV 后易位至细胞质。虽然 siRNA 介导的 PIWIL4 敲低并未显着影响 RSV 复制,但它导致多种细胞因子、趋化因子和生长因子的分泌减少,表明在调节 宿主 先天 免疫应答 中发挥作用。PIWIL4 沉默的 iSAE 细胞的转录组分析显示,在基础条件下和 RSV 感染后基因表达均发生显着变化。Ingenuity 对差异表达基因的通路分析强调了 PIWIL4 在干扰素信号传导、细胞因子产生、应激和代谢反应以及气道重塑通路调节中的作用。PIWIL4 的沉默还导致未感染和感染细胞中 piRNA 表达的整体改变。然而,差异表达piRNA的预测靶标与转录组学鉴定的差异表达基因的重叠有限,这表明PIWIL4在调节气道上皮细胞反应中的功能至少部分独立于piRNA。综上所述,我们的研究揭示了 PIWIL4 在体细胞中的重要作用,并将其定位为气道上皮先天免疫的关键调节因子。更好地了解 PIWIL4 在病原体暴露后影响 宿主 细胞反应的机制可能会确定针对 RSV 以及其他病毒性呼吸道感染的新治疗策略。

papers.title: Clesrovimab in prevention of RSV lower respiratory tract disease: a profile of its use in infants
papers.abstract: Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM, clesrovimab-cfor), a long-acting monoclonal antibody that targets the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion protein, is a useful addition to prophylactic options for RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in the phase 2b/3 CLEVER clinical trial, a single 105 mg dose of clesrovimab, irrespective of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV-associated medically-attended lower respiratory infection (RSV-MALRI), and reduces RSV-associated hospitalizations in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Pharmacokinetic data from the phase 3 SMART trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab was generally well tolerated, with low reactogenicity, and had a similar adverse event profile to placebo (CLEVER) and palivizumab (SMART). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant cause of infant hospitalizations and deaths. Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM), a novel long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds a highly conserved site on the RSV fusion protein, was recently approved in the USA and the EU for the prevention of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in clinical trials, clesrovimab, administered as a single 105 mg dose regardless of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Data from a phase 3 clinical trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children aged < 2 years at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab is well tolerated, with low rates of adverse events. As the second long-acting mAb approved for prevention of RSV disease, clesrovimab represents a useful addition to treatment options for neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season.

Clesrovimab was generally well tolerated, with low reactogenicity, and had a similar adverse event profile to placebo (CLEVER) and palivizumab (SMART). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a significant cause of infant hospitalizations and deaths. Clesrovimab (ENFLONSIATM), a novel long-acting monoclonal antibody (mAb) that binds a highly conserved site on the RSV fusion protein, was recently approved in the USA and the EU for the prevention of RSV-associated lower respiratory tract (LRT) disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. As demonstrated in clinical trials, clesrovimab, administered as a single 105 mg dose regardless of body weight, provides durable protection against RSV disease in neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season. Data from a phase 3 clinical trial supports the efficacy of clesrovimab in infants and children aged < 2 years at increased risk of severe RSV disease. Clesrovimab is well tolerated, with low rates of adverse events. As the second long-acting mAb approved for prevention of RSV disease, clesrovimab represents a useful addition to treatment options for neonates and infants born during or entering their first RSV season.

papers.title: Anakinra in Severe RSV-Associated Autoinflammatory Encephalopathy With Delayed ADEM-Like Changes.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated encephalopathy is an uncommon but potentially devastating complication in children. Increasing evidence suggests that infection-triggered neuroinflammation rather than direct viral invasion underlies neurologic injury in a subset of patients. We describe 2 previously healthy, unrelated children who developed rapidly progressive encephalopathy after RSV infection. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging scan results were normal, but follow-up imaging results showed multifocal white matter lesions consistent with an acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like pattern. Both patients were given refractory to high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and interleukin (IL)-6 blockade. Markedly elevated serum IL-1β levels were documented in one patient. Treatment with the IL-1 receptor antagonist, anakinra, was temporally associated with neurologic and radiologic recovery in both cases. These observations suggest that an IL-1-driven autoinflammatory phenotype may contribute to disease severity in selected children with RSV-associated encephalopathy and highlight the importance of repeat neuroimaging and consideration of targeted immunomodulation in refractory cases.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)相关性脑病是儿童罕见但可能致命的并发症,其潜在机制尚未完全阐明。本研究旨在探讨感染触发的神经炎症是否会导致部分患者出现神经损伤。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为一份病例报告,描述了两名此前健康且无血缘关系的儿童在感染RSV后出现快速进展性脑病。两名患者对包括高剂量皮质类固醇、静脉免疫球蛋白及白细胞介素(IL)-6阻断剂在内的标准治疗均无反应。

elements_zh.main_results: 最初的脑磁共振成像扫描结果正常,但后续成像显示多灶性白质病变,与急性播散性脑脊髓炎样模式一致。在这两种情况下,治疗 联合阿那白滞素与神经系统和放射学恢复均暂时相关。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated encephalopathy is an uncommon but potentially devastating complication in children, and the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. The study was needed to explore whether infection-triggered neuroinflammation contributes to neurologic injury in a subset of patients.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This is a case report describing two previously healthy, unrelated children who developed rapidly progressive encephalopathy after RSV infection. Both patients were refractory to standard therapies including high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and interleukin (IL)-6 blockade.
analysis_en.methods: The authors documented markedly elevated serum IL-1β levels in one patient and administered the IL-1 receptor antagonist anakinra as targeted immunomodulation. Neurologic and radiologic recovery were monitored following treatment.
analysis_en.main_results: Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging scan results were normal, but follow-up imaging showed multifocal white matter lesions consistent with an acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like pattern. Treatment with anakinra was temporally associated with neurologic and radiologic recovery in both cases.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as suggesting that an IL-1-driven autoinflammatory phenotype may contribute to disease severity in selected children with RSV-associated encephalopathy. They highlight the importance of repeat neuroimaging and consideration of targeted immunomodulation in refractory cases.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These observations suggest that IL-1 blockade with anakinra may represent a therapeutic option for children with severe, refractory RSV-associated encephalopathy. The findings underscore the need for vigilance in monitoring for delayed neuroinflammatory complications.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to two case reports, which precludes generalization and does not establish causality. The strength of the evidence is low due to the absence of controls, small sample size, and reliance on temporal associations.

papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated encephalopathy is an uncommon but potentially devastating complication in children. Increasing evidence suggests that infection-triggered neuroinflammation rather than direct viral invasion underlies neurologic injury in a subset of patients. We describe 2 previously healthy, unrelated children who developed rapidly progressive encephalopathy after RSV infection. Initial brain magnetic resonance imaging scan results were normal, but follow-up imaging results showed multifocal white matter lesions consistent with an acute disseminated encephalomyelitis-like pattern. Both patients were given refractory to high-dose corticosteroids, intravenous immunoglobulin, and interleukin (IL)-6 blockade. Markedly elevated serum IL-1β levels were documented in one patient. Treatment with the IL-1 receptor antagonist, anakinra, was temporally associated with neurologic and radiologic recovery in both cases. These observations suggest that an IL-1-driven autoinflammatory phenotype may contribute to disease severity in selected children with RSV-associated encephalopathy and highlight the importance of repeat neuroimaging and consideration of targeted immunomodulation in refractory cases.

papers.title: Perspectives on an Intervention to Increase Confidence in Newborn RSV Immunoprophylaxis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis is efficacious, yet uptake is low in comparison with other recommended newborn interventions. We aimed to identify barriers to and enablers of implementation of an intervention in the well newborn unit to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted individual, semi-structured interviews of purposively sampled clinicians and parents at an urban, quaternary-care hospital well newborn unit between August 13, 2025, and October 22, 2025. Interviews elicited clinicians' and parents' perceptions of RSV immunoprophylaxis, the counseling process, barriers and facilitators, and their perspectives on the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence. Using both deductive and inductive approaches, 4 investigators independently coded the first 2 transcripts in each stakeholder group to identify themes. Two investigators then applied codes to the remaining transcripts, resolving discrepancies by consensus. RESULTS: We interviewed 18 clinicians (5 hospitalists, 3 general pediatricians, 3 obstetricians, 7 nurses/nurse managers) and 24 parents. We identified several themes related to an intervention to increase parental confidence, including barriers and facilitators: (1) trust and mistrust of information; (2) differentiation of RSV immunoprophylaxis from a vaccine; and (3) value of providing both data and personal experiences. We also identified themes related to implementation: (1) support for a tool to augment, but not replace, clinician counseling; (2) use of visuals; (3) accessibility for parents of varying health literacy and languages; and (4) importance of timing. CONCLUSIONS: The identified themes can inform the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on understanding barriers and enablers to implementing an intervention in the well newborn unit to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. The target is respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), specifically RSV-A and RSV-B, with the central question being how to improve parental confidence in RSV immunoprophylaxis for newborns.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on individual, semi-structured interviews conducted with purposively sampled clinicians and parents at an urban, quaternary-care hospital well newborn unit between August 13, 2025, and October 22, 2025. Four investigators independently coded the first 2 transcripts in each stakeholder group using deductive and inductive approaches to identify themes, and then two investigators applied the codes to the remaining transcripts, resolving discrepancies by consensus.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identified several themes related to increasing parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis, including trust and mistrust of information, differentiation of RSV immunoprophylaxis from a vaccine, and the value of providing both data and personal experiences. It also highlighted implementation themes such as support for a tool to augment, but not replace, clinician counseling, use of visuals, accessibility for parents of varying health literacy and languages, and the importance of timing.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report controversies or evidence gaps directly. However, it notes that the findings are based on qualitative interviews, which may not capture the full scope of implementation challenges or provide quantitative data on the effectiveness of the proposed intervention.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The identified themes can inform the design and implementation of an intervention to increase parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis. This includes developing tools that support clinician counseling, incorporating visuals, ensuring accessibility for diverse populations, and timing the intervention appropriately.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores barriers and enablers to increasing parental confidence in newborn RSV immunoprophylaxis through qualitative interviews with clinicians and parents. The study identifies key themes such as trust in information, distinguishing RSV immunoprophylaxis from vaccines, and the importance of combining data with personal experiences. Implementation considerations include supporting clinician counseling with tools, using visuals, ensuring accessibility for diverse populations, and timing the intervention effectively. The findings suggest that these themes can guide the development of targeted interventions to improve uptake of RSV immunoprophylaxis in newborns.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是了解在健康新生儿病房实施干预措施的障碍和推动因素,以提高家长对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。目标是 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV),特别是 RSV-A 和 RSV-B,核心问题是如何提高家长对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评价基于2025年8月13日至2025年10月22日期间对城市四级护理医院新生儿病房有目的地抽样的临床医生和家长进行的个人、半结构化访谈。四名研究人员使用演绎和归纳方法对每个利益相关者组中的前2份记录进行独立编码,以确定主题,然后两名研究人员将代码应用于其余记录,通过协商一致解决差异。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述识别出多个与提升新生儿呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防信心相关的主题,包括对信息的信任与不信任、呼吸道合胞病毒免疫预防与抗病毒药物的区分,以及提供数据与个人经验的价值。综述还强调了实施层面的主题,如支持使用工具辅助(但不替代)临床医师咨询、视觉化呈现、满足不同健康素养水平及语言背景父母的可及性,以及时机选择的重要性。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查不直接报告争议或证据差距。然而,它指出,调查结果基于定性访谈,可能无法捕捉实施挑战的全部范围或提供有关拟议干预措施有效性的定量数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 确定的主题可以为干预措施的设计和实施提供信息,以提高父母对新生儿 RSV 免疫预防的信心。这包括开发支持临床医生咨询的工具、纳入视觉效果、确保不同人群的可及性以及适当地安排干预时间。

papers.title: Impact of Human Adenovirus Co-detection on Disease Severity in Children with Medically Attended Acute Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Human Adenovirus (HAdV) is frequently identified as a cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children and often co-detected with other common respiratory viruses. However, the effect of co-detection on disease severity is not well understood. This study aimed to describe the spectrum and frequency of other respiratory viruses co-detected with HAdV and define the impact of co-detection on HAdV disease severity. Methods Children admitted to the hospital or seen in the emergency department with fever and/or respiratory symptoms <14 days duration were enrolled at 7 sites across the US, from 12/01/2016 through 08/31/2023, as part of the CDC-sponsored New Vaccine Surveillance Network (NVSN). Respiratory specimens were systematically obtained and tested for HAdV and other common viral etiologies of ARI. Demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease severity (hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use) were compared among children with HAdV single detection, HAdV co-detection with other respiratory viral pathogens, and single detection of a non-HAdV virus. Results Of 68,004 children enrolled with a respiratory specimen tested, 4,292 (6.3%) were positive for HAdV; 1,779 (41.4%) of these were HAdV single detections. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV) (43.1%), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (14.7%), and parainfluenza virus (PIV) (7.6%) were the most common viruses co-detected with HAdV and selected for further analysis. HAdV co-detection with these 3 viruses was associated with increased odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use when compared to HAdV single detection. However, the odds of hospitalization and in-hospital oxygen use with HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detection were also increased compared to HAdV single detection. Conclusion HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV was associated with increased disease severity when compared to HAdV single detection. However, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections were also associated with increased severity in comparison to HAdV single detection with these pathogens. Additionally, the increased odds of severe disease seen in HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV single detections was often greater than the increase seen with HAdV co-detection with HRV/EV, RSV, or PIV. This could suggest that the overall severity of these ARIs is being driven primarily by the co-detected viruses, HRV/EV, RSV, and PIV. These results could help guide interpretation of viral testing by clinicians, when multiple viruses are detected. Further research involving asymptomatic and mild HAdV ARI cases, as well as longitudinal studies to determine timing of co-infections, are needed to fully understand the role of HAdV in pediatric ARI of mixed viral etiology.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of co-detection of Human Adenovirus (HAdV) with other respiratory viruses on disease severity in children with acute respiratory infections (ARIs). The research aimed to understand how the presence of multiple viruses affects the severity of HAdV infections. The study was conducted across 7 US sites from 2016 to 2023, involving 68,004 children. HAdV was detected in 6.3% of participants, with 41.4% of these cases being single detections. These results could inform clinical interpretation of viral testing in cases of multiple virus detection. papers.title: Letter to the Editor on: "Nosocomial Respiratory Virus Infections in Hematologic Malignancies: Risk Factors for Progression to Lower Respiratory Tract Infection".
papers.abstract: This Correspondence responds to Oh and colleagues' study on nosocomial respiratory virus infections in hematologic malignancies and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection. We raise three methodological concerns: (1) the landmark analysis used to evaluate URTI-stage ribavirin therapy excludes patients who progressed or died before landmark time points, introducing selection bias by conditioning on a collider; (2) antiviral therapy analyses are severely underpowered (only 15 PIV and 9 RSV treated patients), with wide confidence intervals precluding definitive conclusions and substantial Type II error risk; and (3) combining glucocorticoid exposures from different indications (short-course pulse vs. prolonged therapy) may mask heterogeneous effects on immune function and viral progression. We commend the authors' risk stratification framework while urging cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy data and recommending future prospective studies with adequate sample sizes and refined corticosteroid characterization.

papers.title_zh: 致编辑的信:“血液系统恶性肿瘤中的院内呼吸道病毒感染:进展为下呼吸道感染的危险因素”。
papers.source_body_en: This Correspondence responds to Oh and colleagues' study on nosocomial respiratory virus infections in hematologic malignancies and risk factors for progression to lower respiratory tract infection. We raise three methodological concerns: (1) the landmark analysis used to evaluate URTI-stage ribavirin therapy excludes patients who progressed or died before landmark time points, introducing selection bias by conditioning on a collider; (2) antiviral therapy analyses are severely underpowered (only 15 PIV and 9 RSV treated patients), with wide confidence intervals precluding definitive conclusions and substantial Type II error risk; and (3) combining glucocorticoid exposures from different indications (short-course pulse vs. prolonged therapy) may mask heterogeneous effects on immune function and viral progression. We commend the authors' risk stratification framework while urging cautious interpretation of antiviral efficacy data and recommending future prospective studies with adequate sample sizes and refined corticosteroid characterization.
papers.abstract_zh: 本通讯回应了 Oh 及其同事关于血液系统恶性肿瘤中的院内呼吸道病毒感染以及进展为下呼吸道感染的危险因素的研究。我们提出了三个方法学问题:(1)用于评估 URTI 阶段利巴韦林治疗的里程碑分析排除了在里程碑时间点之前进展或死亡的患者,通过对撞机的调节引入了选择偏差;(2) 抗病毒药物 治疗分析的效力严重不足(仅 15 名 PIV 和 9 名 RSV 治疗患者),置信区间宽,无法得出明确的结论,并且存在大量 II 型错误风险;(3) 结合不同适应症(短程脉冲治疗与长期治疗)的糖皮质激素暴露可能掩盖对免疫功能和病毒进展的异质性影响。我们赞扬作者的风险分层框架,同时敦促谨慎解释 抗病毒药物 疗效数据,并建议未来进行具有足够样本量和精细皮质类固醇特征的前瞻性研究。

papers.title: Changes in Lung Sounds During the Acute Stage of RSV Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.
papers.journal: The Tokai journal of experimental and clinical medicine

papers.title_zh: 婴儿 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 急性期肺音的变化。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的:通过肺音分析评估 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 诱导的急性 毛细支气管炎 呼吸功能随时间的变化。方法:我们回顾性检查了 54 名诊断为急性 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的儿童(中位年龄为 7 个月)肺音参数随时间的变化。我们使用传统方法评估吸气和呼气声音的功率,并使用新的自动分析软件程序分析吸气声音的频率特性。我们检查了住院期间和住院后这些肺音参数随时间的变化,并将这些数据与年龄匹配的健康儿童的数据进行了比较。结果:在 54 名婴儿的 138 个肺音样本中,吸气音和呼气音的力量在发病后 4 天内最强,并随着时间的推移而改善。相比之下,RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 发病后 5 至 10 天观察到吸气音参数的最大变化。RSV急性毛细支气管炎患者的一些肺音参数即使在发病后14天也没有恢复正常。结论:这一发现被认为是婴儿 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 的一个特征,对于 毛细支气管炎 后的管理具有重要意义。

papers.title: Infection-triggered neurological deterioration and immunodeficiency in a case of RNU4ATAC-opathy
papers.abstract: RNU4ATAC-opathy is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a wide clinical spectrum, including brain anomalies, seizures, strokes, immunodeficiency, and cardiac defects. Other manifestations include ophthalmologic, dermatologic, renal, gastrointestinal, auditory, and endocrine involvement. Here, we report the identification of pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants through whole exome sequencing in an infant presenting with microcephaly, growth failure, and immunodeficiency. We describe an 11-month-old infant who had been followed since 4 months of age for growth failure and developmental delay. During follow-up, the patient experienced episodes of neurological deterioration triggered by febrile illnesses associated with SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus infections (RSV) at 9 and 11 months of age, respectively. Immunological evaluation showed normal immunoglobulin levels, a marked reduction in switched memory and memory B cells, impaired T-cell activation, and decreased T-cell subpopulations, suggesting combined immunodeficiency that may have contributed to increased susceptibility to viral infections. Whole exome sequencing subsequently identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in the RNU4ATAC gene, confirming the diagnosis of RNU4ATAC-opathy. RNU4ATAC-opathy should be considered in cases with microcephaly, growth failure, immunodeficiency, and skeletal abnormalities. Our case shows that RNU4ATAC-opathy may present as infection-related encephalopathy, together with combined T- and B-cell dysfunction. Early immunological assessment and timely initiation of prophylactic therapy could play a key role in improving survival. Genetic and immunological evaluations are essential for accurate diagnosis, early intervention, and effective management. Further research is needed to clarify the syndrome’s impact on immune function and guide targeted therapies.

Our case shows that RNU4ATAC-opathy may present as infection-related encephalopathy, together with combined T- and B-cell dysfunction. Early immunological assessment and timely initiation of prophylactic therapy could play a key role in improving survival. Genetic and immunological evaluations are essential for accurate diagnosis, early intervention, and effective management. Further research is needed to clarify the syndrome’s impact on immune function and guide targeted therapies.

papers.source_body_en: RNU4ATAC-opathy is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by a wide clinical spectrum, including brain anomalies, seizures, strokes, immunodeficiency, and cardiac defects. Other manifestations include ophthalmologic, dermatologic, renal, gastrointestinal, auditory, and endocrine involvement. Here, we report the identification of pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants through whole exome sequencing in an infant presenting with microcephaly, growth failure, and immunodeficiency. We describe an 11-month-old infant who had been followed since 4 months of age for growth failure and developmental delay. During follow-up, the patient experienced episodes of neurological deterioration triggered by febrile illnesses associated with SARS-CoV-2 and respiratory syncytial virus infections (RSV) at 9 and 11 months of age, respectively. Immunological evaluation showed normal immunoglobulin levels, a marked reduction in switched memory and memory B cells, impaired T-cell activation, and decreased T-cell subpopulations, suggesting combined immunodeficiency that may have contributed to increased susceptibility to viral infections. Whole exome sequencing subsequently identified compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in the RNU4ATAC gene, confirming the diagnosis of RNU4ATAC-opathy. RNU4ATAC-opathy should be considered in cases with microcephaly, growth failure, immunodeficiency, and skeletal abnormalities. Our case shows that RNU4ATAC-opathy may present as infection-related encephalopathy, together with combined T- and B-cell dysfunction. Early immunological assessment and timely initiation of prophylactic therapy could play a key role in improving survival. papers.abstract_zh: RNU4ATAC 病是一种罕见的常染色体隐性遗传疾病,其临床表现广泛,包括脑异常、癫痫发作、中风、免疫缺陷和心脏缺陷。其他表现包括眼科、皮肤科、肾脏、胃肠道、听觉和内分泌受累。在这里,我们报告了通过对一名患有小头畸形、生长障碍和免疫缺陷的婴儿进行全外显子组测序来鉴定致病性 RNU4ATAC 变异。我们描述了一名 11 个月大的婴儿,该婴儿从 4 个月大起就因生长障碍和发育迟缓而接受随访。在随访过程中,患者分别在 9 个月和 11 个月大时经历了由与 SARS-CoV-2 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 感染 (RSV) 相关的发热性疾病引发的神经功能恶化。免疫学评估显示免疫球蛋白水平正常,转换记忆和记忆 B 细胞显着减少,T 细胞活化受损,T 细胞亚群减少,表明联合免疫缺陷可能导致对病毒感染的易感性增加。全外显子组测序随后鉴定出 RNU4ATAC 基因中的复合杂合致病性变异,证实了 RNU4ATAC 疾病的 诊断。对于小头畸形、生长障碍、免疫缺陷和骨骼异常的病例,应考虑 RNU4ATAC 病。我们的病例表明,RNU4ATAC 病可能表现为感染相关脑病,并伴有 T 细胞和 B 细胞功能障碍。早期免疫学评估和及时开始预防性治疗可以在提高生存率方面发挥关键作用。遗传和免疫学评估对于准确的 诊断、早期干预和有效的管理至关重要。需要进一步的研究来阐明该综合征对免疫功能的影响并指导靶向治疗。
