Evidence shows that people aged over 65 who are immunosuppressed or have chronic respiratory disease have a similar risk of being hospitalised to those aged over 75 who are already offered the vaccine free from the NHS. The offer will run from September and will help protect eligible adults who are more likely to experience severe illness if they catch the virus. RSV is a common virus that can cause serious health problems, including bronchiolitis and pneumonia, particularly in older people and babies. Each year, it leads to between 700 and 1,000 hospital admissions among people aged over 75 in Wales, as well as up to 9,000 GP appointments. The RSV vaccine is already routinely offered to all adults aged 75 and over. Evidence from a new study led by Public Health Wales, working with other UK teams, found that RSV vaccination cut the risk of ending up in hospital from RSV by 75 per cent among adults aged 75 to 79 during the winter of 2024–25. The study also found that RSV-related hospital admissions fell by more than 13 per cent among the eligible 75–79 age group between October 2024 and April 2025, despite the programme being in its early stages. Expanding the offer to higher-risk people aged 65 to 74 will help prevent further serious illness and hospital admissions, while also easing pressure on GPs and hospitals during the winter months. Dr Christopher Johnson, Head of the Vaccine Preventable Disease Programme at Public Health Wales, said: “We have strong evidence that the RSV vaccine works. It reduces the risk of ending up in hospital with RSV by around 75 per cent, helping protect older adults from serious illness. “By expanding free access to more people aged 65 to 74 who are at higher risk, we can help keep more people healthy and out of hospital, particularly during the winter months when RSV is most dangerous. “If you’re eligible, I strongly encourage you to get vaccinated when you’re invited.” For more information, visit Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination information. Request a sample and discover the recent advances in Respiratory Syncytial Virus treatment drugs: https://www.delveinsight.com/sample-request/respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-pipeline-insight?utmsource=openpr&utm_medium=pressrelease&utm_campaign=kspr What is Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)? Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) is a highly contagious respiratory virus that primarily infects the upper and lower respiratory tract, including the nose, throat, and lungs. It is one of the most common causes of respiratory illness worldwide, particularly affecting infants, young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. RSV spreads through respiratory droplets, direct contact with infected individuals, or contact with contaminated surfaces followed by touching the eyes, nose, or mouth. RSV infections typically occur seasonally and are a major cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in young children. The symptoms of RSV usually appear within 4-6 days after exposure and may initially resemble mild upper respiratory tract infections. Common symptoms include runny nose, cough, sneezing, fever, wheezing, and reduced appetite. Infants may experience irritability, poor feeding, and breathing difficulties. In severe cases, particularly among high-risk populations, RSV can lead to bronchiolitis and pneumonia, with symptoms including rapid breathing, chest retractions, wheezing, and cyanosis. The virus infects respiratory epithelial cells and uses its fusion (F) and attachment (G) proteins to enter cells and form syncytia. This process leads to inflammation, mucus production, airway obstruction, and impaired gas exchange. Diagnosis is generally based on clinical presentation and can be confirmed using laboratory tests such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from nasal or throat swabs. Treatment is mainly supportive and may include hydration, antipyretics, oxygen therapy, and ventilatory support in severe cases. Preventive strategies include hygiene practices, vaccination in certain populations, and prophylactic monoclonal antibodies for high-risk infants. Emerging Respiratory Syncytial Virus Drug Profiles Deuremidevir Hydrobromide: Simcere Pharmaceutical Group Deuremidevir Hydrobromide (VV116) is an orally administered small-molecule antiviral drug developed by Vigonvita Life Sciences in collaboration with Simcere Pharmaceutical Group for viral infections, including Respiratory Syncytial Virus. The drug is a nucleoside analog with broad-spectrum antiviral activity and works by inhibiting viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), thereby blocking viral RNA replication and preventing the spread of infection. The therapy has received a Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the China National Medical Products Administration for RSV infection. Deuremidevir Hydrobromide has completed Phase II development and is currently in Phase III clinical trials for RSV infection. S-337395: Shionogi S-337395 is a novel orally administered small-molecule antiviral drug candidate being jointly developed by Shionogi and UBE Corporation for Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The drug is designed as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L protein) inhibitor, blocking the activity of the RSV L protein, which is essential for viral genome transcription and replication. S-337395 has received Fast Track designation from the US Food and Drug Administration and has shown positive results in Phase II clinical trials. Currently, the drug is in Phase II clinical development for RSV. SCTV02: Sinocelltech Ltd. SCTV02 is a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate developed for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The vaccine uses a stabilized prefusion RSV F protein designed to induce neutralizing antibodies and prevent viral entry into host cells. The therapy is being developed for prophylactic prevention of RSV infection, particularly among vulnerable populations such as infants, elderly individuals, and those at high risk of severe disease. Currently, SCTV02 is in Phase I/II clinical trials. EuRSV: Eubiologics EuRSV is a recombinant protein-based RSV vaccine candidate being developed by EuBiologics for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The vaccine uses a liposome nanoparticle-based platform incorporating RSV antigens, including the F protein, combined with immune-enhancing adjuvants. EuRSV is designed to stimulate humoral and cellular immune responses and is being developed for prophylactic use against RSV infection. Currently, EuRSV is in Phase I clinical development. RSV spreads through respiratory droplets, direct contact with infected individuals, or contact with contaminated surfaces followed by touching the eyes, nose, or mouth. RSV infections typically occur seasonally and are a major cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in young children. The symptoms of RSV usually appear within 4-6 days after exposure and may initially resemble mild upper respiratory tract infections. Common symptoms include runny nose, cough, sneezing, fever, wheezing, and reduced appetite. Infants may experience irritability, poor feeding, and breathing difficulties. In severe cases, particularly among high-risk populations, RSV can lead to bronchiolitis and pneumonia, with symptoms including rapid breathing, chest retractions, wheezing, and cyanosis. The virus infects respiratory epithelial cells and uses its fusion (F) and attachment (G) proteins to enter cells and form syncytia. This process leads to inflammation, mucus production, airway obstruction, and impaired gas exchange. Diagnosis is generally based on clinical presentation and can be confirmed using laboratory tests such as polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from nasal or throat swabs. Treatment is mainly supportive and may include hydration, antipyretics, oxygen therapy, and ventilatory support in severe cases. Preventive strategies include hygiene practices, vaccination in certain populations, and prophylactic monoclonal antibodies for high-risk infants. Emerging Respiratory Syncytial Virus Drug Profiles Deuremidevir Hydrobromide: Simcere Pharmaceutical Group Deuremidevir Hydrobromide (VV116) is an orally administered small-molecule antiviral drug developed by Vigonvita Life Sciences in collaboration with Simcere Pharmaceutical Group for viral infections, including Respiratory Syncytial Virus. The drug is a nucleoside analog with broad-spectrum antiviral activity and works by inhibiting viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp), thereby blocking viral RNA replication and preventing the spread of infection. The therapy has received a Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the China National Medical Products Administration for RSV infection. Deuremidevir Hydrobromide has completed Phase II development and is currently in Phase III clinical trials for RSV infection. S-337395: Shionogi S-337395 is a novel orally administered small-molecule antiviral drug candidate being jointly developed by Shionogi and UBE Corporation for Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The drug is designed as an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L protein) inhibitor, blocking the activity of the RSV L protein, which is essential for viral genome transcription and replication. S-337395 has received Fast Track designation from the US Food and Drug Administration and has shown positive results in Phase II clinical trials. Currently, the drug is in Phase II clinical development for RSV. SCTV02: Sinocelltech Ltd. SCTV02 is a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate developed for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The vaccine uses a stabilized prefusion RSV F protein designed to induce neutralizing antibodies and prevent viral entry into host cells. The therapy is being developed for prophylactic prevention of RSV infection, particularly among vulnerable populations such as infants, elderly individuals, and those at high risk of severe disease. Currently, SCTV02 is in Phase I/II clinical trials. EuRSV: Eubiologics EuRSV is a recombinant protein-based RSV vaccine candidate being developed by EuBiologics for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus infection. The vaccine uses a liposome nanoparticle-based platform incorporating RSV antigens, including the F protein, combined with immune-enhancing adjuvants. EuRSV is designed to stimulate humoral and cellular immune responses and is being developed for prophylactic use against RSV infection. Currently, EuRSV is in Phase I clinical development. Among US veterans, 2025-2026 mRNA-1345 vaccination is associated with a reduced risk for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-confirmed acute respiratory illness (ARI) hospitalization, according to study findings published in Vaccine. Since its approval in May 2024, mRNA-1345 (mRESVIA) has been shown to prevent RSV-associated lower respiratory tract disease in adults in clinical trials. Real-world data on use of the vaccine, particularly against severe RSV infection outcomes, are scarce. To bridge this knowledge gap, researchers conducted a retrospective, test-negative, case-control study using electronic health record data from the Veterans Health Administration. The analysis included 91,397 veterans aged 50 years and older who had an ARI-related encounter and underwent RSV testing between September 2025 and April 2026; only 1.4% had received the mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine. These findings highlight the public health importance of RSV vaccination programs in populations at risk of severe outcomes. From that larger cohort, the researchers matched 3673 individuals who tested positive for RSV to 14,566 control individuals who tested negative for the virus. Within the subset of patients who were hospitalized, mean patient age was approximately 74 years, and more than 90% were men. Nearly all (98%) patients had at least 1 chronic condition, including 84% with hypertension and approximately 50% with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or diabetes. Multivariable conditional logistic regression was employed to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) against RSV-associated medically attended ARI, a composite outcome that incorporated hospitalizations, emergency department/urgent care (ED/UC) visits, and outpatient visits. Within the hospitalized cohort, fewer than 5 patients who tested positive for RSV and 49 patients who tested negative had received mRNA-1345 vaccine, reflecting an estimated adjusted VE of 85% (95% CI, 39-96). For RSV-associated medically attended ARI, VE was 65% (95% CI, 45-77), with VE estimates of 57% (95% CI, 28-74) and 71% (95% CI, 19-90) for protection against ED/UC visits and outpatient visits, respectively. The researchers noted that these figures are similar to those seen in prior studies of protein-based RSV vaccines. Study limitations include the low number of individuals who both tested positive for RSV and were vaccinated against the virus in the subset of hospitalized patients, leading to imprecise estimates of effect size; possible residual confounding stemming from the observational design; potential misclassification of RSV vaccination status; possible bias introduced by the test-negative design; and reduced generalizability. The researchers concluded, “These findings highlight the public health importance of RSV vaccination programs in populations at risk of severe outcomes.” Disclosure: This study was supported by a research award from Moderna. Multiple study authors declared affiliations with biotech, pharmaceutical, and/or device companies. Please see the original reference for a full list of disclosures. analysis.brief_en: A study published in Vaccine on September 1, 2026, found that mRNA-1345 RSV vaccine is associated with reduced risk for RSV-confirmed acute respiratory illness (ARI) hospitalization among US veterans aged 50 and older. Among hospitalized patients, the estimated adjusted vaccine effectiveness (VE) against RSV-associated hospitalization was 85% (95% CI, 39-96). news.content: MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Log In Register Subscribe Log In MORE FROM MCKNIGHT’S MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Subscribe Job Board Directory Clinical Latest News Care Delivery & Staff Development Clinical Programs & Prevention Patient Conditions & Therapies Business Latest News Finance & Investment Operations & Asset Management Workforce & Marketing Payment Workforce Regulatory Legal Regulations & Compliance Quality & Workforce Standards Technology Automation & Administrative Tech Clinical & Care Technologies Data, Security & Analytics McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit Opinions & Features Editors’ Columns Guest Columns Marketplace Columns The Brighter Side Series and Special Coverage Column Submission Guidelines Live and Virtual Events McKnight’s Pinnacle Awards McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit McKnight’s Women of Distinction Conference Coverage Webinars Online Forums Product Theaters Workforce Development Forums Resources Newsmakers Podcasts Market Leaders Podcasts E-Books E-Newsletters Magazine Partner content Videos Whitepapers Workforce Development Guide McKnight’s LTC News – Awards Won Clinical Daily News RSV vaccine helps prevent hospitalizations, secondary outcomes, massive nursing home study finds Foster Stubbs (Photo: South_agency/Getty Images) August 31, 2026 Share › Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email Print (Photo: South_agency/Getty Images) The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine showed a vaccine effectiveness (VE) of 73% against RSV-associated hospitalization among Medicare beneficiaries in nursing homes, according to an August study published in JAMA Internal Medicine. The study examined data on 597,430 Medicare beneficiaries in the Common Working File and Minimum Data Set (MDS). The primary outcome tracked was RSV-associated hospitalization; secondary outcomes included RSV-associated death or severe RSV-associated outcomes requiring an intensive care unit or critical care unit admission. The results showed that VE against hospitalization among beneficiaries aged 65 to 74 years was 60%; among beneficiaries 75 years or older, it was 75%. Among immunocompromised beneficiaries, VE was 61%, and VE was 76% among immunocompetent beneficiaries. Meanwhile, VE against RSV-associated death was 56%, and against severe RSV-associated outcomes, VE was 59%. The lower estimated VE found in this study, compared to previous similar studies, could be attributed to the increased probability of RSV hospitalization in nursing home settings in contrast with community-dwelling older adults, authors said. Authors also note that because the study observed only Medicare Part A and B beneficiaries residing in nursing homes, the sample size may not be completely generalizable to the overall US population of people 65 years or older residing in nursing homes or other subpopulations. “Our results indicate RSV vaccination provided protection against RSV-associated hospitalization and other severe RSV-associated outcomes among nursing home residents during the 2023-2024 RSV season,” authors said. “In June 2024, CDC’s ACIP strengthened its RSV recommendations to recommend all adults 75 years and older and adults aged 60 to 74 years who are at increased risk for severe RSV (including nursing home residents) receive 1 dose of RSV vaccine. news.content_zh: 发表在《JAMA Internal Medicine》上的一项研究发现,RSV 疫苗 对美国疗养院居民中与 RSV 相关的住院治疗和其他严重后果显示出有效性 (VE)。该研究检查了 597,430 名医疗保险受益人的数据,结果显示,65 至 74 岁人群中 VE 抵抗住院治疗的比例为 60%,75 岁或以上人群中为 75%。在免疫功能低下的受益人中,VE 为 61%,在免疫功能正常的受益人中,VE 为 76%。疫苗 还表现出 56% 的 VE 可以预防 RSV 相关死亡,59% 的 VE 可以预防严重后果。作者指出,与之前的研究相比,VE 较低可能是由于疗养院环境中 RSV 住院的可能性较高。CDC 的 ACIP 于 2024 年 6 月更新了其建议,将 75 岁及以上的成年人和 60 至 74 岁的严重 RSV 风险较高的人纳入其中,并于 2025 年进一步扩大建议范围,将 50 至 59 岁的个人纳入其中。然而,该研究的样本量可能无法完全推广到更广泛的美国疗养院老年人群体或其他亚人群。

Bradley Peterson, MD, discusses when pediatricians should consider adding a second treatment for pediatric anxiety and why improvement may continue well beyond the first 3 months of therapy. The AAP's updated clinical report revises screening timelines, ferritin thresholds, and treatment protocols for pediatric iron deficiency and iron deficiency anemia. CDC has declared the Nara Organics infant botulism outbreak over; genetic testing ties it to the 2025 ByHeart outbreak. Bradley Peterson, MD, discusses how treatment preferences, access, tolerability, and patient characteristics can guide pediatric anxiety care when CBT and medication provide similar overall benefits. Lori Handy, MD, says vaccine conversations with hesitant families should prioritize trust, follow-up, and the benefits for the individual child. CBT and fluoxetine both reduced pediatric anxiety, while starting with CBT before adding medication showed advantages on several outcomes. The FDA has approved Tivicay PD (dolutegravir) to treat HIV-1 in newborns from birth, based on IMPAACT 2023 pharmacokinetic and safety data. FDA De Novo authorization establishes Avulux lenses as an option for migraine-associated light sensitivity in patients aged 12 years and older. FDA authorized Abbott's Libre Duo 10 Day, the first wearable that continuously tracks glucose and ketones, for patients 2 and older with diabetes. FDA approved nipocalimab (Imaavy) for wAIHA in patients 12 and older, based on Phase 2/3 ENERGY trial data on durable hemoglobin response. Nine societies outline 6 domains of hospital-level sepsis strategies, from rapid blood culture diagnostics to daily toothbrushing protocols. Phase 3 data show lebrikizumab improved skin clearance, itch, and quality of life in children with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. Pediatric psychiatric diagnoses and treatment rose above prepandemic levels, with notable increases in medication initiation and care among girls

news.content_zh: 该文,由《当代儿科学》于2026年8月27日发布,探讨呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)对儿科医疗的持续影响。文章强调了RSV在三重大流行后1年急诊科更新中的重要性,指出RSV仍是一项重大健康问题。文中聚焦儿科医生在即将到来的呼吸道病毒季节中应了解的RSV相关知识,并强调提高认识与做好准备的必要性。然而,文中未提供具体病例数、死亡数或暴露人数。该文作为针对医疗保健提供者的一般性指导,提供了儿童RSV管理的见解,但未详述具体干预措施或结果。内容基于对过往事件与当前策略的回顾,但未呈现新数据或确认性发现。

Kappe, PhD: Pioneering Vaccine Solutions To Global Diseases More Faculty News Social Media Last week we celebrated the White Coat Ceremony for the Class of 2030! 🩺 👏 As these future physicians donned their white coats for the first time, they made a commitment to excellence, compassion, and service. We're honored to welcome this exceptional group to our community! 🧬 DNA: UNLOCKED! Students at our Mini Med School program explored the fascinating world of DNA with Dr. Michelle Giglio and Dr. Joe Receveur from our Institute for Genome Sciences. Students discovered how genetic information makes each person unique. ✂️🍓 Homicides in Baltimore in 2026 are at record lows. This is the result of community programs, law enforcement, gun violence prevention programs, and healthcare providers working together. The teams at University of Maryland Medical System's Shock Trauma Center have been on the front lines of this journey. We received $3 million to establish two new endowed professorships!👏 These endowed professorships in gene & cell therapy and pediatric cardiac surgery will bring world-class physician-scientists to the University of Maryland Golisano Children's Hospital and University of Maryland, Baltimore. Welcome Dr. Enrico M. Novelli! Dr. Enrico M. Novelli, MD, MS, an internationally recognized expert in sickle cell disease, will be joining the School of Medicine as Director of the Program in Sickle Cell Disease and Professor in the Department of Medicine, Division of Hematology/Oncology. Baltimore Street, Seminar Room, 1010 IGS & CAMRI Seminar Series 9Sep “Chikungunya Arthritis Therapeutics” 12:00 PM | Shock Trauma Auditorium Grand Rounds - Infectious Diseases 2026 State of the School Address Please join Dean Mark T. Gladwin as he delivers the 2026 State of the School Address. Date: September 16, 2026, Time: 3:30 PM Location: Leadership Hall View All Events Just the Facts 501.2M Total grants and contracts for our researchers in FY 2025 12th Among all public medical schools Ranked by the AAMC 3.84 Average applicant GPA to the MD Program Did you Know? We achieved an historic, first-ever pig-to-human heart transplant in 2022. Did you Know? We were the first public medical school in the U.S. Did you Know? We were the first to build a teaching hospital and offer a residency program. Did you Know? We invented the field of “Shock Trauma.” Did you Know? We were the first to discover the relationship between insects and disease. Did you Know? We are one of the largest organ transplant centers in the U.S. Did you Know? We made vaccine breakthroughs around the world for COVID-19, Ebola, Zika, cholera, MERS/SARS, influenza, malaria and typhoid. Did you Know? We were the first to use a drone to deliver a kidney for transplantation. Did you Know? We were the first to test a unique RNA COVID-19 vaccine. More Facts About UMSOM The University of Maryland School of Medicine gave me the space to make lifestyle medicine the foundation of my practice — and taught me that being a good doctor starts with being well myself, so I can show up for my patients fully present, empathetic, and human-centered. Laila Abujuma, MD, ’26 MD Graduate About Baltimore ▸ Our Location

Language Language Close KR CN Open Search bar Search field News Search Remove icon Search icon Dim Industry · IT Bio Health Is National Support for RSV Immunization Cost-Effective? by Lee Sungmin Published 27 Aug.2026 10:04(KST) Updated 27 Aug.2026 11:03(KST) open/close Share Language Text Size Print Pfizer's Maternal Vaccine Joins Sanofi and MSD Preventive Injections Available, But Fully Self-Funded Options for preventing respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in infants and young children are expanding. In addition to the introduction of two types of long-acting prophylactic antibodies administered directly to infants, a vaccine for pregnant women has also been launched. As the methods of prevention are diversifying, there is increasing discussion about the need to consider not only efficacy but also factors such as cost, target recipients, and the impact on healthcare expenditures. According to industry sources on August 27, two types of long-acting RSV prophylactic antibodies for infants—Sanofi·AstraZeneca's “Beyfortus (nirsevimab)” and “Enfloncia (clessrovimab)” from MSD Korea—are currently competing in the domestic market. Pfizer's RSV vaccine “Abrysvo” has also become an option through its administration to pregnant women to protect infants. While Beyfortus and Enfloncia involve administering fully developed antibodies directly to infants, Abrysvo works by vaccinating pregnant women, enabling them to pass on protective antibodies to the fetus. ChatGPT Generated Image View original image RSV is a common acute respiratory virus among infants and young children, with most children becoming infected at least once before the age of two. In most cases, infection presents with cold-like symptoms, but in relatively younger infants or those in high-risk groups, it can progress to lower respiratory tract infections such as bronchiolitis and pneumonia, sometimes requiring hospitalization. Particularly during the early months of life, infants have narrower airways and underdeveloped immune systems, leaving them more vulnerable to severe disease caused by RSV infection. The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends the introduction of maternal vaccines or long-acting monoclonal antibodies for infant RSV prevention, advising countries to also consider cost-effectiveness, availability, and expected vaccination rates. Once similar levels of preventive efficacy have been established, it becomes increasingly important to determine which method best fits a country’s healthcare environment and financial circumstances. Expanding access to preventive measures ultimately requires an assessment of the benefits relative to financial investment. According to a study conducted last year by Professor Seo Hye-Seon’s team at Kyung Hee University College of Pharmacy, administering nirsevimab to all infants under one year of age as well as high-risk children under two years was compared to the conventional strategy focusing only on high-risk groups. The results showed a reduction in medical costs related to hospitalization and emergency room visits, as well as decreased productivity loss for caregivers. More than 90% of the total health improvement was observed in full-term infants under one year old. Similar analyses have been reported in other countries. In Italy, many regions found that the savings in hospital costs resulting from reduced RSV hospitalizations exceeded the cost of administering the prophylactic antibodies. In Japan, research indicated that expanding the target group for prevention to include all infants could further reduce disease burden and healthcare expenditures. According to estimates, for every 10 percentage point increase in the use of nirsevimab, approximately 2,780 additional lower respiratory tract RSV cases could be prevented. analysis.location_and_population: South Korea, infants and young children.
analysis.event: Discussion on the cost-effectiveness of national support for RSV immunization, including maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies for infants, is ongoing. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) is considering government support after reviewing disease burden and financial implications.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: A study by Kyung Hee University College of Pharmacy showed a reduction in medical costs related to hospitalization and emergency room visits, as well as decreased productivity loss for caregivers. In Italy, savings from reduced hospitalizations exceeded the cost of prophylactic antibodies. In Japan, expanding prevention to all infants could reduce disease burden and healthcare expenditures. The potential cost savings per 10 percentage point increase in nirsevimab use is approximately 2,780 additional cases prevented.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The National Immunization Program (NIP) is currently vaccine-focused, and separate considerations are needed for monoclonal antibody administration. The KDCA has stated that a decision on government support will be made only after a comprehensive review of disease burden and expected government expenditure. The prophylactic antibodies for healthy infants are not yet covered by insurance.

analysis.brief_en: The article discusses the cost-effectiveness of national support for RSV immunization in South Korea, focusing on maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies for infants. It highlights that while preventive measures like Beyfortus and Abrysvo are expanding, the National Immunization Program (NIP) remains vaccine-focused. A study by Kyung Hee University College of Pharmacy found that administering nirsevimab to all infants under one year of age could reduce medical costs and caregiver productivity loss. In Italy, savings from reduced hospitalizations exceeded the cost of prophylactic antibodies, and similar findings have been reported in Japan. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) is considering government support for these measures after reviewing disease burden and financial implications. However, the prophylactic antibodies for healthy infants are not yet covered by insurance, and further analysis is needed to determine the best approach for South Korea's healthcare system.

In Italy, savings from reduced hospitalizations exceeded the cost of prophylactic antibodies, and similar findings have been reported in Japan. The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) is considering government support for these measures after reviewing disease burden and financial implications. However, the prophylactic antibodies for healthy infants are not yet covered by insurance, and further analysis is needed to determine the best approach for South Korea's healthcare system.

elements_zh.location_and_population: 韩国,婴幼儿。
elements_zh.event: 关于国家支持 RSV 免疫(包括孕产妇 疫苗 和婴儿单克隆抗体)的成本效益的讨论正在进行中。韩国疾病控制和预防机构 (KDCA) 在审查疾病负担和财务影响后正在考虑政府支持。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 庆熙大学药学院的一项研究表明,与住院和急诊室就诊相关的医疗费用减少了,护理人员的生产力损失也减少了。在意大利,住院治疗减少所节省的费用超过了预防性抗体的费用。在日本,将预防扩大到所有婴儿可以减轻疾病负担和医疗保健支出。尼塞韦单抗 使用量每增加 10 个百分点,潜在的成本节省大约可减少 2,780 个额外案例。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 国家免疫计划(NIP)目前以疫苗为重点,单克隆抗体给药需要单独考虑。KDCA 表示,只有在全面审查疾病负担和预期政府支出后才会做出政府支持的决定。健康婴儿的预防性抗体尚未纳入保险范围。

news.content_zh: 文章讨论了韩国国家支持 RSV 免疫接种的成本效益,重点关注孕产妇 疫苗 和婴儿单克隆抗体。它强调,虽然 Beyfortus 和 Abrysvo 等预防措施正在扩大,但国家免疫计划 (NIP) 仍然以 疫苗 为重点。庆熙大学药学院的一项研究发现,对所有一岁以下的婴儿服用 尼塞韦单抗 可以降低医疗费用和护理人员生产力损失。在意大利,减少住院治疗所节省的成本超过了预防性抗体的成本,日本也报告了类似的结果。韩国疾病控制和预防机构 (KDCA) 在审查疾病负担和财务影响后,正在考虑政府对这些措施的支持。然而,健康婴儿的预防性抗体尚未纳入保险范围,需要进一步分析以确定适合韩国医疗保健系统的最佳方法。

Nirsevimab May Reduce Invasive Pneumococcal Disease in Infants: Study Subscribe to Notifications Written By : Dr Riya Dave Medically Reviewed By : Dr. Kamal Kant Kohli Published On 2026-09-01 02:15 GMT | Update On 2026-09-01 08:50 GMT A French retrospective study suggests that nirsevimab (Beyfortus), used to prevent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, may also reduce the risk of invasive pneumococcal disease. Infants immunized with nirsevimab were about 35% less likely to be hospitalized for invasive pneumococcal disease through 9 months of age, highlighting its potential as a complementary strategy alongside pneumococcal vaccination, especially as non-vaccine pneumococcal serotypes continue to emerge. The study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases by Ines F. and colleagues. To investigate if there is any reduction in the frequency of hospitalized cases of IPD with nirsevimab immunization, the study conducted a review of all liveborn infants in metropolitan France born between February 6, 2023, and January 31, 2024. Children who had nirsevimab immunization within their first year of life were considered part of the immunized cohort, while children without immunization who matched their birth month were part of the non-immunized cohort. The outcome used in this study was the admission to the hospital for confirmed IPD 6 months after the patient was included in the study. To control for confounders and even out the baseline clinical characteristics of both immunized and non-immunized groups, researchers used propensity score matching with IPTW. The effectiveness of the vaccine was calculated using the following formula: effectiveness=100% × (1 − odds ratio [OR]). Key findings: Among 608,641 total births live during the study period, 527,971 satisfied inclusion criteria, including 119,435 infants (22.6%) who were given nirsevimab. A total of 112 IPD cases occurred in the six months' follow-up; in immunized cohort, there were 17 cases (14.2 per 100,000) whereas in non-immunized cohort, there were 95 cases (23.3 per 100,000). IPTW corrected analysis showed that nirsevimab was connected with significant odds reduction 36% for hospitalization due to IPD 6 months post-vaccination (OR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.46-0.82). The effectiveness remained consistently high and there was 34% reduction in odds for IPD by 9 months after vaccination (OR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.85). In summary, children less than 12 months who had received nirsevimab vaccination were observed to have reduced susceptibility to IPD for up to 6 months after the procedure. The study has revealed an unexpected yet critical additional benefit of RSV monoclonal antibody prophylaxis other than the protection from the virus infection itself. The increased use of RSV immunization among infants by public health institutions will enable proper healthcare planning during the season with an understanding of this cross-protection effect on infant mortality rates. Reference: Fafi, I., Valtuille, Z., Kaguelidou, F., Levy, C., Cohen, R., Angoulvant, F., Bizot, E., Bonacorsi, S., Birgy, A., Pontual, L. Effectiveness of nirsevimab immunisation on invasive pneumococcal disease in children nationwide in France: an observational cohort study. news.content: MENU Home News Digi-Wrap Sign Up About ► About Practice Business Our Team Contact us For Advertisers Sign in Home News Digi-Wrap Sign Up About About Practice Business Our Team Contact us For Advertisers Sign in Management Health & Patient Care Health Tech Practice Operations Recruit and Retain Legal & Compliance Live It Follow us on Twitter Follow us on Facebook Follow us on LinkedIn Email us HomePractice OperationsRead Again: RSV Vaccine Expansion: What It Means For Practice Operations Read Again: RSV Vaccine Expansion: What It Means For Practice Operations August 27, 2026 Practice Operations The expansion of the RSV vaccination programme to older adults and care home residents presents new operational and planning priorities for GP practice managers CREDIT: This is an edited version of an article that originally appeared in England NHS Primary care teams are set to play a key role in delivering an expanded vaccination programme aimed at protecting some of the most vulnerable patients from serious respiratory illness. In April, the NHS widened access to the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, making all adults aged 80 and over, as well as residents in care homes for older adults, eligible. This expansion brings approximately 3 million additional people into the programme, significantly increasing the cohort practices may need to support. Clinical Importance and Patient Risk RSV is a common respiratory virus that can lead to severe complications in older adults, including pneumonia, bronchitis, and exacerbations of chronic conditions such as COPD. These complications often result in hospital admissions and increased pressure on secondary care services. In the UK, RSV is responsible for around 9,000 hospitalisations annually among people aged over 75. A single vaccine dose offers protection lasting several years, making it a valuable preventative intervention. Programme Continuity and Existing Cohorts The expanded rollout builds on the initial programme launched in September 2024, which targeted adults aged 75 to 79 and those turning 75. These groups remain eligible if they have not yet received the vaccine. Additionally, pregnant women from 28 weeks gestation continue to be offered the RSV vaccine to protect newborns from severe respiratory infections. Practices should ensure these cohorts are not overlooked amid the expansion. Access and Delivery Channels Patients can book vaccinations through GP practices, and practice teams should ensure booking systems are updated accordingly. Care home staff will play a role in coordinating vaccinations for residents, while selected community pharmacies are also offering the vaccine in some areas. Practice managers should consider communication strategies to inform eligible patients, including targeted messaging, recall systems and collaboration with local healthcare partners. Key Actions for Practice Managers Review and adjust clinic capacity to meet increased demand Ensure adequate vaccine stock and cold chain management Coordinate with care homes and community pharmacies Update patient recall and invitation systems Support staff with clear guidance on eligibility and delivery pathways Effective planning and coordination will be essential to maximise uptake and reduce RSV-related complications in high-risk populations. Nation.Cymru staff More people in Wales at increased risk of serious illness from a common respiratory infection are to be offered a vaccine. Adults aged 65 to 74 who are immunosuppressed or have chronic respiratory disease will become eligible for the RSV vaccine under a time-limited extension of the NHS programme during September. The vaccine is already routinely offered to people aged 75 and over, as well as during pregnancy to help protect babies during their first months of life. Public Health Wales said evidence showed people aged over 65 with weakened immune systems or chronic respiratory conditions faced a similar risk of hospitalisation from RSV as those aged over 75. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) usually causes a mild illness such as a cough or cold in adults, but can lead to pneumonia and other serious health problems in older and more vulnerable people. It can also worsen existing heart and lung conditions. In Wales, RSV is estimated to cause between 700 and 1,000 hospital admissions among people aged over 75 each year, as well as up to 9,000 GP appointments. The NHS vaccination programme was introduced in Wales in September 2024. A study led by Public Health Wales alongside other UK teams subsequently found vaccination reduced the risk of hospital admission from RSV by around 75% among people aged 75 to 79 during the winter of 2024-25. RSV-related hospital admissions among that age group also fell by more than 13% between October 2024 and April 2025, despite the vaccination programme still being in its early stages. Dr Christopher Johnson, head of the Vaccine Preventable Disease Programme at Public Health Wales, said: “We have strong evidence that the RSV vaccine works. It reduces the risk of ending up in hospital with RSV by around 75 per cent, helping protect older adults from serious illness. “By expanding free access to more people aged 65 to 74 who are at higher risk, we can help keep more people healthy and out of hospital, particularly during the winter months when RSV is most dangerous. “If you’re eligible, I strongly encourage you to get vaccinated when you’re invited.” Share this: Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Click to email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email Support our Nation today For the price of a cup of coffee a month you can help us create an independent, not-for-profit, national news service for the people of Wales, by the people of Wales. 吾乃喵大人 MedSci原创 发表于上海 呼吸道合胞病毒尼塞韦单抗急性病毒性毛细支气管炎 呼吸新前沿 企业/ 关注 互相关注 尼塞韦单抗全国普及可显著降低婴幼儿毛细支气管炎的就诊、住院及重症风险,有效减轻患儿病情严重程度,是防控婴幼儿RSV感染的高效手段。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 急性病毒性毛细支气管炎是新生儿及1岁以内婴儿首要住院病因,其中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染占全部病例的60%以上,是全球婴幼儿下呼吸道感染的核心致病元凶。全球每年约3400万5岁以下儿童发生RSV相关下呼吸道感染,造成330万例住院及超12万例死亡,低收入地区及合并基础疾病的婴幼儿为高危人群。既往临床仅有的RSV预防药物为帕利珠单抗,该药作用周期短、需每月给药、费用高昂,且仅适用于少数高危早产儿,仅能覆盖25%的重症RSV病例,绝大多数健康足月患儿缺乏有效防护手段。 长效单克隆抗体尼塞韦单抗(nirsevimab)可单次给药,为婴幼儿首个RSV流行季提供长效防护,已在多国获批应用。意大利于2024—2025年首次全国推广尼塞韦单抗预防项目,但该国医疗体系存在区域自治特点,各地区药物投放时间、婴幼儿筛查召回策略存在显著异质性,全国层面的真实应用效果、疾病流行特征及患儿病情变化数据仍处于空白状态。基于此,本研究依托意大利全国儿科研究网络,开展多中心真实世界研究,系统评估尼塞韦单抗全国普及的临床价值。 Medicine:小分子定向分化液下培养的人鼻腔上皮用于呼吸系统疾病建模 该液下分化模型兼具传统平面培养的可及性和规模化优势以及气道上皮的细胞复杂性,支持在原发性纤毛运动障碍、囊性纤维化和呼吸道合胞病毒感染等多种呼吸系统疾病中进行功能性表型分析、治疗药物测试和抗病毒评价。 JAMA子刊:尼塞韦单抗对不同月龄婴幼儿毛细支气管炎的保护差异 对RSV流行季前出生的婴儿实施后期召回接种尼塞韦单抗,可使临床诊断的全因毛细支气管炎风险降低 45%-48%。 Lancet子刊:减少半数住院!RSV 母体疫苗真实世界表现印证预防价值 母体 RSVpreF 免疫可有效降低婴儿首个 RSV 流行季的住院与重症风险,优化接种时机、保障公平可及将进一步放大疫苗的公共卫生价值,为全球 RSV 防控策略提供了坚实的真实世界证据支撑。 Lancet Microbe:法国全国性研究警示,RSV-B 突破感染中尼塞韦单抗耐药率达12.5% 这项迄今为止规模最大的尼塞韦单抗耐药真实世界研究,全面揭示了 RSV-B 耐药的分子特征和临床规律,为保障单克隆抗体的长期有效性、优化全球 RSV 防控体系提供了重要科学支撑。 超 25 万婴儿真实世界证据:尼塞韦单抗有效降低 RSV 住院,需警惕耳鼻喉细菌感染及次年哮喘住院信号 尼塞韦单抗在连续两个不同毒株主导的 RSV 流行季中,均能稳定降低婴儿首年 RSV-LRTI 住院风险,为其跨季节的临床价值提供了坚实的真实世界证据。 Journal of Global Health:五岁以下儿童RSV相关急性中耳炎 这项研究发现超过四分之一的RSV感染会并发急性中耳炎,同时在急性中耳炎患儿样本中RSV检出率也较高,且绝大多数RSV阳性中耳液样本同时存在细菌感染。 Lancet子刊:拉美儿童 RSV 住院负担核心驱动因素 在拉美三国三甲医院中,重症 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染造成了沉重的经济与健康负担,而疾病严重程度(以 ICU 住院为代表)而非病毒本身,是决定单例住院成本与健康损失的核心因素。 警惕呼吸道合胞病毒!孟加拉农村婴幼儿半岁内风险最高,早产儿更危险 孟加拉农村婴幼儿 RSV 感染负担突出、季节波动明显、高危人群集中,亟需以证据为基础开展针对性预防,降低重症与医疗系统压力,守护儿童健康。 警惕!阳性率升至近九个月以来最高,增速在各类呼吸道病原体中位居首位,已经出现危重病例 2026 年夏季新冠、流感、鼻病毒、RSV、腺病毒、肠道病毒多病原体同步流行,校园聚集性疫情增多。区分各病毒临床特点,流感发病 48 小时内尽早抗病毒,对症治疗配合通风、洗手等综合防护。 吾乃喵大人 MedSci原创 发表于上海 呼吸道合胞病毒尼塞韦单抗急性病毒性毛细支气管炎 呼吸新前沿 企业/ 关注 互相关注 尼塞韦单抗全国普及可显著降低婴幼儿毛细支气管炎的就诊、住院及重症风险,有效减轻患儿病情严重程度,是防控婴幼儿RSV感染的高效手段。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 急性病毒性毛细支气管炎是新生儿及1岁以内婴儿首要住院病因,其中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染占全部病例的60%以上,是全球婴幼儿下呼吸道感染的核心致病元凶。全球每年约3400万5岁以下儿童发生RSV相关下呼吸道感染,造成330万例住院及超12万例死亡,低收入地区及合并基础疾病的婴幼儿为高危人群。既往临床仅有的RSV预防药物为帕利珠单抗,该药作用周期短、需每月给药、费用高昂,且仅适用于少数高危早产儿,仅能覆盖25%的重症RSV病例,绝大多数健康足月患儿缺乏有效防护手段。 长效单克隆抗体尼塞韦单抗(nirsevimab)可单次给药,为婴幼儿首个RSV流行季提供长效防护,已在多国获批应用。意大利于2024—2025年首次全国推广尼塞韦单抗预防项目,但该国医疗体系存在区域自治特点,各地区药物投放时间、婴幼儿筛查召回策略存在显著异质性,全国层面的真实应用效果、疾病流行特征及患儿病情变化数据仍处于空白状态。基于此,本研究依托意大利全国儿科研究网络,开展多中心真实世界研究,系统评估尼塞韦单抗全国普及的临床价值。 analysis.brief_en: This news report discusses a study published in a Lancet subjournal evaluating the clinical value of nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody, in reducing the hospitalization burden of RSV-associated bronchiolitis in infants. The study, conducted in Italy, is a multicenter retrospective cohort study assessing the nationwide impact of nirsevimab. RSV infection is a leading cause of hospitalization in infants under one year old, with over 34 million cases globally each year, resulting in 3.3 million hospitalizations and more than 120,000 deaths. The study highlights that nirsevimab can provide long-term protection with a single dose, significantly reducing the use of medical resources such as emergency visits, general ward admissions, and PICU intubations. However, the implementation of the drug in Italy has shown regional disparities in drug distribution and screening strategies, leaving national-level data on its effectiveness and disease dynamics incomplete. The findings suggest that nirsevimab could be a highly effective tool in preventing RSV infections in infants, particularly in high-risk populations such as those with preterm birth or congenital heart disease.

By Austin Johnson Published: Aug. 31, 2026 at 4:50 AM CDT Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google QUINCY (WGEM) - The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates that COVID-19 cases are growing in Missouri and Illinois. The Adams County Health Department (ACHD) is offering tips on preventing sickness and minimizing risk. The ACHD is encouraging vaccination for those whose bodies allow it as it looks to prevent a rise in illness this fall. The Adams County Health Department is encouraging vaccination for those whose bodies allow it as it looks to prevent a rise in illness this fall.(WGEM) “There’s lots of research to show that they work, and it protects you if you get a vaccine,” said Tara Bealor, health protection director. “It doesn’t necessarily mean you’re not gonna get sick, but it will lessen the severity of it. It will decrease your risk of being hospitalized and having severe illness.” Health department officials said people can get both a COVID and flu shot on the same day, with one shot in the left arm and the other in the right arm. “It’s important for all of us to remember that when making a choice about vaccines, yes, it is about you and your family, but it is also about the community,” Bealor said. It is not clear whether cases are rising in Iowa because the state does not estimate an epidemic trend. According to the CDC cases are not as severe compared to one year ago. To lower the risk of sickness, including COVID, flu, RSV or a common cold, health officials recommend proper and frequent handwashing for at least 20 seconds, whether sick or not. According to the National Library of Medicine, wearing a mask reduces the chances of bacterial droplets entering the nose or mouth. All Illinois health departments no longer track COVID cases. According to the latest CDC guidance, people who contract the virus can return to normal activities after symptoms disappear and they are fever-free for 24 hours without medication. People experiencing trouble breathing or chest pain are recommended to call their family doctor. Copyright 2026 WGEM. All rights reserved. Expanded testing and treatment services help make CVS Pharmacy a convenient destination for seasonal care. WOONSOCKET, R.I., Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CVS Health® (NYSE: CVS) today announced that updated 2026-2027 flu vaccines are now available at CVS Pharmacy® and MinuteClinic® locations nationwide. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), annual flu vaccination is one of the most effective ways to help reduce the risk of flu-related illness and complications. Patients can schedule vaccination appointments online at CVS.com, MinuteClinic.com or through the CVS Health app. Walk-in appointments are also available at CVS Pharmacy and MinuteClinic locations. As families prepare for the fall and winter respiratory virus season, CVS Health offers a range of services designed to support preventive care and help patients manage seasonal illnesses. In addition to flu vaccination, patients can access testing and treatment options at select CVS Pharmacy and MinuteClinic locations, providing connected care before, during and after illness. With health care professionals serving communities across the country, CVS Health remains committed to helping patients stay protected throughout the season. Most Americans plan to get vaccinated this flu season According to a survey of U.S. consumers commissioned by CVS Health1, 63% of Americans say they are likely to receive a flu vaccine this season. That is similar to the last two years when 63% said they were planning to get a flu shot in 2025 and 62% said they were planning to get a flu shot in 2024. Among those planning to get vaccinated: 68% plan to get a flu vaccine by the end of October. 34% of consumers want a flu shot before the illness is spreading widely; 28% want to get vaccinated before spending time with someone who may be vulnerable to influenza, like a newborn, older adult or someone who is ill; and 24% want to get the flu shot to help avoid missing school, work or other responsibilities. Habit and personal protection are the most significant motivators among people who intend to get the flu shot, with 39% of people saying they get a flu shot every year and 37% saying they get a flu shot to protect their health or their family's health. 43% of consumers say they plan to get a flu shot at a retail pharmacy, while 34% plan to get the flu shot at a doctor's office. "Getting vaccinated is one of the simplest and most effective steps people can take to help protect themselves and those around them during flu season," said Amy Compton-Phillips, MD, Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer, CVS Health. "As respiratory viruses continue to circulate each year, it's important that people and families have convenient access to trusted health care professionals who can answer questions, provide recommended vaccinations and help them stay healthy throughout the season." CDC recommends annual flu vaccination for nearly everyone The CDC recommends that everyone ages six months and older, with rare exceptions, receive an annual flu vaccine, with September and October generally being ideal times for vaccination ahead of peak flu activity. The updated 2026-2027 vaccine is designed to help protect against flu strains that experts anticipate will be most common this season. To further support patients during respiratory illness season, participating CVS Pharmacy locations are offering convenient testing options, including a combination test that can detect Influenza A, Influenza B, and COVID-19 with a single swab. In states where pharmacists are authorized to both test and treat eligible patients for flu and COVID-19, patients can receive an assessment and, when appropriate, treatment recommendations during the same visit. Participating states include California, Colorado, Idaho, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, Nebraska, South Dakota, Tennessee, Washington, Wisconsin, and Wyoming. Patients can learn more about testing options by visiting CVS.com. MinuteClinic also offers testing for Influenza A, Influenza B, and COVID-19 in all clinic locations. "Patients want health care that is easy to access and fits into their busy lives," said Sid Tenneti, Senior Vice President and Interim President, Pharmacy and Consumer Wellness, CVS Health. "Whether someone is looking to get vaccinated, needs help understanding symptoms, or is seeking testing and treatment options, CVS Pharmacy is committed to providing connected, convenient care in the communities we serve." Convenient vaccination options for patients Vaccination appointments are available seven days a week at CVS Pharmacy locations, including those inside Target stores, as well as at MinuteClinic. Patients can schedule appointments online at CVS.com, MinuteClinic.com or through the CVS Health app. The online scheduler allows patients to book appointments at CVS Pharmacy and MinuteClinic for up to four people at once and receive multiple CDC-recommended vaccinations during a single visit, including flu, COVID-19, hepatitis B, RSV, MMR, and shingles vaccines. Organizations can also partner with CVS Health to host vaccination clinics at the workplace or within their communities, meeting patients where they are and making it easier to access recommended vaccinations. In addition to vaccinations, MinuteClinic offers evaluation and treatment for select seasonal illnesses, including flu-like symptoms, with testing available for eligible patients. More information and appointments are available at MinuteClinic.com. Year-round access to recommended vaccinations CVS Pharmacy and MinuteClinic offer more than 15 commonly recommended vaccinations throughout the year to help protect against preventable diseases. Patients who receive any CDC-recommended vaccine at CVS Pharmacy will also receive a $5 off $20 to use on in-store purchases.2 Most preventive vaccines are available at no cost through many insurance plans, including Medicare Part B coverage for eligible vaccines. Out-of-pocket costs may vary based on insurance coverage and vaccine type. Patients who receive a CDC-recommended vaccination at CVS Pharmacy may also be eligible for promotional savings and ExtraCare Rewards®, subject to program terms and conditions. Video and photo assets from CVS Pharmacy and MinuteClinic are available here. About CVS Health CVS Health is a leading health solutions company simplifying health care one person, one family and one community at a time. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had approximately 9,000 retail pharmacy locations, more than 1,000 walk-in and primary care medical clinics and a leading pharmacy benefits manager with approximately 87 million plan members. The Company also serves an estimated 37 million people through a broad range of health insurance products and related services. The Company's integrated model uses personalized, technology driven services to connect people to simply better health, increasing access to quality care, delivering better outcomes, and lowering overall costs. Appointments scheduled online will receive the coupon after vaccination. Limit one per customer per vaccine visit. For vaccines that require multiple doses, the coupon will be given with vaccine series completion. Merchandise coupon redeemable at CVS Pharmacy® and Longs Drugs® for one-time use. ExtraCare® card required to receive savings. Terms and conditions apply. See coupon for details. Coupon barcode number must be provided to redeem online. $5 savings applied to total qualifying minimum purchase of $20 (after other coupons and discounts are applied). Coupon shall not be issued in Arkansas, New Jersey or New York, or at MinuteClinic® locations in Arkansas, Massachusetts, New Jersey or New York. Coupon cannot be redeemed at CVS Pharmacy® at Target, CVS Pharmacy® at Schnucks® or at MinuteClinic® locations. This offer is solely made by CVS® and not connected with any vaccine manufacturer. HSE South West is encouraging parents across Cork to protect their babies this winter with free immunisation against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).       Amy Campbell HSE South West is encouraging parents across Cork to protect their babies this winter with free immunisation against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). RSV is a common winter virus that can cause serious illness in infants, particularly during their first season. Immunisation is provided as a single dose of ‘nirsevimab’, giving babies immediate protection and helping to prevent severe infection and hospitalisation. Dr Anne Sheahan, regional director of public health at HSE South West, said: “RSV immunisation has been a gamechanger for protecting babies from serious illness during the winter months. “It is very safe, highly effective, and gives babies protection at a time when they are particularly vulnerable to RSV. Here in the South West, we strongly encourage parents of every eligible baby in Cork and Kerry to take up the offer of free RSV immunisation. “It is a simple step that can make a very real difference in keeping babies well and out of hospital this winter.” Babies born between September 1, 2026, and February 28, 2027, will be offered RSV immunisation in maternity hospitals before discharge, where possible. Babies born between March 1 and August 31, 2026, can receive RSV immunisation through participating GP practices. Eligible babies at higher risk of serious RSV illness will be offered immunisation through a specialist pathway. Evaluation from the 2025/2026 programme found high uptake across eligible groups and substantial reductions in RSV-related emergency department presentations, hospitalisations, and intensive care unit admissions. news.title_zh: 科克父母被敦促考虑用于婴儿的‘颠覆性’呼吸道合胞病毒尼塞韦单抗
news.source_body_en: Cork parents are being encouraged to consider the 'gamechanger' RSV vaccine for their babies, as it has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of severe RSV illness during the winter months. The HSE South West is promoting free immunisation for eligible infants, with doses administered in maternity hospitals before discharge or through GP practices. Evaluation from the 2025/2026 programme indicated high uptake and substantial reductions in RSV-related emergency department visits, hospitalisations, and ICU admissions. The vaccine, known as 'nirsevimab', provides immediate protection and is described as very safe and highly effective. The initiative targets babies born between September 1, 2026, and February 28, 2027, as well as those at higher risk of serious RSV illness. The article highlights the importance of this immunisation in keeping babies healthy and out of hospital during the winter season.

news.content: Overseas Contract Orders Reach Nearly RMB27.4 mn and R&D Translation Gains Momentum, with the AEPC Platform Reshaping the R&D Paradigm for Equine Polyclonal Antibody Interim Results Highlights Key Financial Indicators Revenue amounted to RMB83.3 mn; gross profit amounted to RMB60.3 mn, representing a gross profit margin of approximately 72.3%; Adjusted net profit (net profit excluding one-off items such as listing expenses and tax rate differential adjustments) amounted to approximately RMB38.7 mn; R&D expenses amounted to RMB11.0 mn, representing a year-on-year increase of 18.6% and accounting for 13.2% of revenue; Key Pipeline Progress Human tetanus antitoxin (Human TAT): As of the end of the Period, total sales volume was approximately 9,577,000 units, comprising approximately 5,911,000 units in the domestic market and approximately 3,666,000 units in overseas markets. The Group successfully won multiple overseas government tender orders, with cumulative contracted orders of approximately 6,859,000 units and a total contract value of approximately RMB27.4 mn; Veterinary Tetanus Antitoxin (Veterinary TAT): As of (the date of the announcement), the product had obtained marketing approval and officially commenced production, becoming the Group's first veterinary product to achieve industrialization; Pregnant Mare Serum Gonadotropin (PMSG): As of the date of the announcement, the commercialization of PMSG APIs and formulations were progressing, and the Group is accelerating the upgrade and construction of a PMSG production line designed in compliance with the Chinese Veterinary Pharmacopoeia and EU GMP standards; Clinical Development (as of the date of the announcement) By pipeline category, the Group had 9 candidate products, including 6 human pharmaceutical products and 3 veterinary pharmaceutical products; Key progress: 2 human pharmaceutical product pipelines, namely Agkistrodon Halys Antivenom and Agkistrodon Acutus Antivenom, initiated Phase II clinical trials; and 2 veterinary pharmaceutical products, namely Bursal Peptide Injection and Pig Spleen Transfer Factor, obtained the new veterinary drug registration approval; Translation of Research Outcomes Phased breakthroughs achieved in patent accumulation, academic publications and accreditations: The Group held 52 granted patents, completed the publication of 2 breakthrough research results in international biomedical journals during the Period; The Group was recognized as the "Advanced Intelligent Factory (先進智能工廠)" and the Specialized, Sophisticated, Distinctive and Innovative "Little Lighthouse Enterprise (小燈塔企業)" in Jiangxi Province, and was awarded the Second Prize of the Jiangxi Provincial Technological Invention Award (江西省技術發明獎二等獎); Platform-level development integrating AI and technology was upgraded across two core segments of the industry chain, namely antigen development and antibody preparation: The Group established an "AI+ fusion protein mRNA antigen" development platform, enhancing the efficiency of antigen design and subsequent product development; The Group developed an equine F(ab')2 process platform based on immobilized dual recombinant endopeptidases and, for the first time, established a synergistic dual-endopeptidase "one-pot" process based on molecular mechanism design. At the laboratory research stage, the Group applied two purification technologies, namely ion exchange chromatography and pathogen-specific affinity chromatography, achieving mean increases in specific activity of relevant products of approximately 30% and 400%, respectively; Next Steps The Group will comprehensively upgrade and build the "AEPC Platform", integrating R&D, production, sales and governance through AI and digital capabilities to form a closed loop, promote resource synergy and commonality reuse across its dual-wheel pipelines, reduce the marginal costs of pipeline development and translation, and continuously unlock the platform-level value of equine polyclonal antibody technology. HONG KONG, Aug. 31, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jiangxi Institute of Biological Products Inc. and its subsidiaries (collectively, "JIANGXI BIO" or the "Group") (stock code: 6915.HK) announced its unaudited interim results for the six months ended June 30, 2026 (the "Period"). During the Period, adhering to its dual-wheel synergistic pipeline strategy of "human pharmaceutical products + veterinary pharmaceutical products" and leveraging its rare integrated full-industry-chain advantages in antiserum, the Group achieved phased progress in core product market share, clinical pipeline advancement, platform technology breakthroughs and international market expansion. Resilient Profitability with Accelerated Momentum for Mid-to-Long-Term Translation Overseas Contracted Orders for Products Rise to Approximately RMB27.4 mn; R&D Investment Increases by Nearly 19% Y-o-Y In the first half of 2026, the global pharmaceutical industry was undergoing structural adjustment, impacted by geopolitical uncertainties, trade frictions and continued strengthening of compliance regulations. The resource allocation across the industry has become more prudent. Facing a complex external environment, the Group leveraged the clinical essential demand for Human TAT, its fully integrated industry chain advantages and its global market presence to maintain steady development in its core business, expanding sales channels and increasing contracted orders through differentiated marketing strategies to enhance its operational resilience. During the Period, the Group recorded revenue of approximately RMB83.3 mn, representing a decrease of 16.5% year-on-year ("Y-o-Y"); gross profit amounted to RMB60.3 mn, representing a gross profit margin of approximately 72.3%; and profit for the Period amounted to approximately RMB14.4 mn. Excluding one-off items such as listing expenses and tax rate differential adjustments, adjusted net profit amounted to RMB38.7 mn, representing a decrease of 21.7% Y-o-Y. The changes in results were primarily attributable to the combined effects of: (i) an increase in R&D expenses; (ii) adjustments to relevant national tax policies; (iii) a decrease in investment income; (iv) an increase in depreciation of fixed assets; and (v) one-off listing expenses. During the Period, the Group continued to increase its R&D investment. R&D expenses amounted to approximately RMB11.0 mn, representing an increase of 18.6% Y-o-Y and accounting for 13.2% of revenue, and were primarily used to advance innovative pipeline development and platform technology upgrades, providing strong support for the translation of mid-to-long-term R&D outcomes and sustainable growth. During the Period, sales revenue from the Group's core product, Human TAT, amounted to approximately RMB77.5 mn, with sales volume of approximately 9,577,000 units, of which approximately 5,911,000 units were sold in the domestic market and approximately 3,666,000 units in overseas markets. The Group continued to promote the synergistic distribution of ampoule and vial packaging formats and expand end markets, actively strengthening its operational resilience. In the domestic market, terminal coverage reached 27,100 medical institutions (including 1,720 tertiary medical institutions). The vial-packaged products were listed on the centralized pharmaceutical procurement platforms in 32 provinces and cities across China and achieved supplementary follow-up bidding under inter-provincial alliance procurement in 26 provinces and cities. In overseas markets, the Group completed market registrations and renewals in four markets, namely India, the DR Congo, Zanzibar and Ghana, and successfully won government tender orders from Ethiopia, Togo and Mongolia. During the Period, the Group's cumulative overseas contracted orders reached 6,859,000 units, with a total contract value of approximately RMB27.4 mn. Steady Progression of the Dual-wheel Pipeline AI+ Technology Platform Upgrade Activates the Pipeline Innovation Engine During the Period, the Group advanced the integration of AI and machine learning technologies into antiserum R&D and production, enabling its technologies to evolve toward greater precision, enhanced stability, higher purity and increased platform scalability. The application boundaries of its products were expanded to four major fields: bio-toxicosis, viral infections, bacterial infections and immunomodulation, while continuously extending into equine plasma-derived product applications. As of the date of the announcement, the Group had commercialized 3 products, while 5 candidate products had entered new stages of clinical research or commercialization. The development progress of specific pipelines and innovative products is as follows: Bio-toxicosis: have initiated Phase II clinical trials with Agkistrodon Halys Antivenom with the first patient enrolled and dosed; completed Phase I clinical trials for Agkistrodon Acutus Antivenom and initiated Phase II clinical trials; and accelerated the antigen design and product development for Polyvalent Snake Antivenom through using AI-assisted antigen design and mRNA-LNP delivery technologies; Viral infections: process research was advanced for Equine Rabies Immunoglobulin F(ab')2 and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Antibody candidates. Equine immunization validation for the RSV Antigen had been completed and successfully induced high-titer antibody responses. On the veterinary pharmaceutical products side, the new drug registration application for Recombinant Porcine Interferon α is in progress; Bacterial infections: For Equine Anti-Drug-Resistant Bacteria F(ab')2, the Group completed the recognition of key targets in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by polyclonal antibodies and validated their potential for virulence neutralization. On the veterinary pharmaceutical products side, the Group enriched its veterinary anti-infective product portfolio building upon the commercialization of Veterinary TAT; Immunomodulation: Phased breakthroughs were achieved in veterinary pharmaceutical products, with Pig Spleen Transfer Factor and Bursal Peptide Injection obtaining the New Veterinary Drug Registration Certificates. Their commercialization will be advanced successively; Equine plasma-derived product applications: With the commercialization of PMSG as a key entry point, the Group accelerated production line upgrades and global market penetration. Meanwhile, it accelerated the exploration of the development potential of multiple functional components in equine plasma and extended into diversified application scenarios such as veterinary regenerative medicine, research and diagnostic reagents, driving the multi-component development and multi-scenario translation of biological resources and expanding the Group's commercialization potential. Accelerated Translation of R&D Translations Unlocking the Potential of the Equine Polyclonal Antibody Platform, and archiving Promising Laboratory Validation Data for Purification Technologies The continued expansion of the pipeline is underpinned by the Group's equine polyclonal antibody technology platform. Compared with a single-target pathway, equine polyclonal antibodies are characterized by multi-epitope recognition, rapid response and scalable production. Combined with the diverse immunoglobulin repertoires and large-body-size advantages of horses, this technology provides an important foundation of high protective efficacy, high throughput and cost-effectiveness for the Group's pipeline R&D and industrialization. During the Period, the Group deepened its core technological advantages in antiserum and empowered the integrated digital and intelligent upgrade of R&D and manufacturing through AI+, transitioning from the traditional "passive screening" paradigm to "proactive intelligent design" and building a more differentiated technological barrier at the platform level for equine polyclonal antibody. In antigen development, the Group established an "AI+ fusion protein mRNA antigen" development platform, further enhancing the efficiency of antigen design and subsequent product development. In antibody preparation, the Group developed an equine F(ab')2 process platform based on immobilized dual recombinant endopeptidases IdeZ2 and IdeS and, for the first time, established an IdeZ2+IdeS synergistic dual-endopeptidase "one-pot" process based on molecular mechanism design, thereby enhancing R&D and preparation efficiency. During the Period, the Group also achieved phased validation of cutting-edge research results. At the laboratory research stage, the Group applied two purification technologies, namely ion exchange chromatography and pathogen-specific affinity chromatography, achieving mean increases in specific activity of relevant products of approximately 30% and 400%, respectively, compared with existing products (the average specific activity of products as of December 31, 2025 was 82,000 IU/gp, while the Chinese Pharmacopoeia Standard was 45,000 IU/gp). The relevant results provide innovative support for the quality upgrade of existing products and the engineering, standardization and platform-based development of subsequent pipelines. Next Step Comprehensively Upgrading the "AEPC Platform" to Develop the Clinical Value of Dual-wheel Pipelines Across Five Directions Looking ahead, the Group proposes to upgrade and build the "AEPC Platform (馬源多克隆抗體全產業鏈數智平台)" upon its existing integrated full-industry-chain advantages. Anchored by four core segments: Antigen Development, Equine Immunization, Plasma Processing and Commercialization. The platform horizontally integrates key segments of the industry chain and vertically extends across R&D, production, sales and governance, forming an interconnected innovation closed loop. Leveraging this platform, the Group will accelerate resource synergy and commonality reuse across the full industry chain under its dual-wheel pipeline strategy, reduce the marginal costs of pipeline development and translation, consolidate its leadership in Human TAT while cultivating incremental global markets, and deepen the development of its equine polyclonal antibody technology platform. On this basis, the Group will advance the integration of AI, biotechnology and the antiserum industry, broaden the boundaries of antiserum indications, deepen the clinical value of equine plasma-derived products, explore diversified commercial opportunities, and bring more high-quality Chinese antiserum products to patients worldwide. About Jiangxi Institute of Biological Products Inc. Jiangxi Institute of Biological Products Co., Ltd. (the "Group") is a globally leading platform-based biopharmaceutical enterprise integrating the full industrial chain of antiserum products. By 2025 sales volume, the Group was the world's largest provider and exporter of human tetanus antitoxins (Human TAT) and had maintained a dominant position in China's Human TAT market for 19 consecutive years. Its products are exported to over 30 countries and regions worldwide and have cumulatively served more than one billion patients globally. Pursuing its mission of "Make Quality Medicine for People Worldwide", and leveraging the industry's extremely high entry barriers, rare full-industry-chain integration and leading technological advantages, the Group has established a dual-wheel synergistic pipeline of "human pharmaceutical products + veterinary pharmaceutical products". It focuses on four fields: bio-toxicosis, viral infections, bacterial infections and immunomodulation, while continuously extending into equine plasma-derived product applications. In 2026, the Group upgraded and built the "AEPC Platform", integrating R&D, production, sales and governance across the full-industry-chain through AI and digital capabilities, deepening the underlying technological barriers of equine polyclonal antibody, providing safer and more effective solutions to address critical unmet medical and animal health prevention and treatment needs globally, and contributing Chinese strength to global public health. For more information, please visit https://en.jxswzp.cn/. SOURCE Jiangxi Institute of Biological Products Inc
